stories.Headline: Baidu head Robin Li warns that artificial intelligence could be a bubble
stories.Summary:
Robin Li, the head of Chinese technology giant Baidu, warned that artificial intelligence could be a bubble on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. He spoke during a panel discussion with business leaders in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen. This event took place ahead of talks between the world's top two economies regarding the sensitive AI sector. Li stated that the adoption of this technology is not boosting profits for most companies. He described the current global landscape for artificial intelligence as being in an urgent situation.

The APEC meeting in Shenzhen hosts talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. counterpart Donald Trump on Thursday, November 19. These leaders will discuss AI risks and the need for cooperation despite a fierce rivalry in the field. Baidu, based in Beijing, reported its sixth straight drop in quarterly revenue on Monday, November 16, 2026. The company faces headwinds in online marketing and a domestic consumer slump that drags on its advertising cash flows. Nvidia is also reporting quarterly results on November 17, following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang.

Robin Li said that the expansion of AI into the application layer has arguably fallen short of expectations. He questioned if companies are seeing higher revenues or increased profits after adopting the technology. Li noted that for most companies, the answer to that question is no. He warned that the concern about an AI bubble could become a reality if this is not addressed. He acknowledged that while Baidu has tangible results in its AI strategy, the company still faces significant challenges.

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva told AFP in October that losing confidence in AI returns could lead to worldwide financial stability risks. She warned that tanking stock market valuations could occur if investors lose faith in future returns from these investments. Market jitters have increased because Jensen Huang quit as Nvidia CEO last week after admitting to an affair. This scandal reportedly involved a suspected Chinese spy and has increased scrutiny of how Chinese companies access powerful chips. These chips are used to train AI systems despite the existence of strict U.S. export rules.

Baidu has made an aggressive push into artificial intelligence in recent years and is sometimes called the Google of China. The company has recently unveiled new AI processors and supercomputing products to further its goals in the sector. Nvidia rejected an offer from Jensen Huang to return as CEO despite pressure coming from Silicon Valley. The U.S. and China are both pushing for AI safety steps while chip tensions loom over the summit. These developments occur as the global investment boom in artificial intelligence comes under serious question.

President Xi Jinping and Donald Trump will meet on Thursday to discuss the risks posed by artificial intelligence. The two tech powerhouses are facing calls for cooperation despite their rivalry and the ongoing tensions over chips. The articles leave open whether the two leaders will reach an agreement on AI safety or cooperation. It remains unclear if the reported financial stability risks mentioned by Georgieva will manifest in the global markets. The future of AI profitability for most companies remains a central point of uncertainty for the industry.

stories.Headline: Concerns about the fairness of the evaluation are growing as artificial intelligence (AI) glasses ap..
stories.Summary:
The Korea Energy Engineering University, also known as KENTECH, announced on November 23 that it will hold creativity interviews on November 30. This decision follows growing concerns about the fairness of college entrance essay tests due to the appearance of artificial intelligence glasses. The university aims to reduce the possibility of cheating by directly checking the process applicants use to find their answers. This year's early admission process saw a competition rate of 31.14 to 1, which the school claims is the highest since it opened.

The evaluation requires applicants to spend 30 minutes preparing an answer before engaging in 15 minutes of face-to-face questions with two interviewers. These interviews focus on the thinking process rather than fixed answers, allowing students to use high school concepts to propose logical solutions. For the 2026 school year, applicants had to recommend the best of four virtual technologies based on five items, including safety and user experience. Interviewers check if the final conclusion remains consistent without contradiction when they present new conditions or different perspectives.

Jang Kwang-jae, who heads the Admissions Student Affairs Department at KENTECH, stated that evaluations in the AI era must check how students explain judgments. He believes that the university can evaluate the competence of students who have prepared sincerely through these creativity interviews. The school also plans to strengthen the management of test sites by controlling the import of electronic devices. By using continuous face-to-face questioning, the university believes it will be difficult for students to cheat using answers made by artificial intelligence.

stories.Headline: Google lets schools opt out of AI in its apps and search
stories.Summary:
Google announced a new artificial intelligence policy for schools that use its apps, providing settings for opting in or out of AI products on student accounts, and schools that reject AI in the classroom entirely can also turn off search, according to a commentary published by CNA. The piece was prompted by headlines claiming there is no longer a way to use Google search without AI, which followed comments from Google's vice president for education, Chris Phillips, who told the New York Times that search and AI are deeply integrated. The commentary explains that AI algorithms have ordered Google's search results for many years and that every part of a search engine, from crawling and indexing to spam detection and ranking, likely involves some form of machine learning. It draws a distinction between that underlying AI and generative AI, meaning systems trained on enormous amounts of data that can produce new content from prompts.

The commentary says that at the time of writing there is no official switch letting Google users disable AI Overviews and other generative AI features, but that appending "&udm=14" to a search request link makes results default to the Web tab without AI Overviews and other snippets. It notes this must be added manually in the address bar, which is not always practical, so people have built browser plugins and ways to automate the step, and in Mozilla Firefox and Chromium browsers such as Brave, Chrome and Opera on desktop a custom search engine can add the parameter on every search. It also lists other search engines, including DuckDuckGo, Brave Search and Ecosia, which it says provide a non-AI mode that deactivates AI summaries by default and in some cases offer the option to filter out AI-generated images. The commentary adds that only a few organisations can maintain a web index at large scale, with Google's and Microsoft Bing's the most popular worldwide, while Brave Search runs from an independent engine and DuckDuckGo combines multiple sources.

The commentary attributes the pushback against AI to personal, ethical or environmental reasons and says that searchers who see AI Overviews are accessing fewer sources overall, while overreliance on AI is a well-known phenomenon in which users may trust an answer without verifying whether it is correct. It says the large language model behind AI summaries is built on an astonishing amount of training data but is not updated as frequently as the web search index, and that links in AI summaries are associated with the answer after it is generated, a step that can also make mistakes. The piece describes search features as not static, with developers, engineers and information retrieval researchers constantly tinkering and improving them. It does not say what Google or the other companies plan to do next.

stories.Headline: Most Croats cautious about AI application in healthcare, education: poll - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Croatian Radiotelevision released an HRejting poll on Saturday, November 21, 2026, showing that most citizens are cautious about artificial intelligence. The survey took place from November 13 to 17 and gathered responses from 1,000 different people. Results indicated that 41 percent of respondents have only superficial knowledge, while 37 percent use tools like ChatGPT. Ten percent use these technologies at an advanced level, and 12 percent remain completely unfamiliar with them.

The data shows that over 60 percent of people reject medical diagnoses generated by AI because they value human empathy. About 65 percent of the participants oppose replacing teachers with algorithms, though one-third see AI as a helpful teaching aid. In the judiciary, finance, and traffic sectors, 65 percent trust humans more due to intuition and morality. Only 8 percent would entrust AI with traffic decisions, and 5.5 percent would use it for financial matters.

Respondents expressed significant concerns regarding the long-term impact of relying on these automated systems. Nearly half of the people surveyed believe the biggest risks are the loss of independence and critical thinking. Another 20 percent of the participants expressed worries about data misuse and the loss of personal privacy. Additionally, 70 percent of the respondents stated that artificial intelligence cannot be a true friend to a human.

Articles.Title: Most Croats cautious about AI application in healthcare, education: poll - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Singapore fintechs outpace global peers in AI adoption rates
stories.Summary:
A report released on Wednesday, November 19, 2026, revealed that fintech companies in Singapore are leading the way in adopting artificial intelligence. This study was based on a survey of 100 fintech leaders and detailed interviews with 10 senior industry practitioners. The research team conducted their fieldwork between July and September 2026 to gather these findings. Most of these firms have already integrated the technology into their current business operations.

The data shows that 86 percent of Singapore fintechs have deployed AI, which is higher than the 65 percent rate for Singapore financial institutions. This adoption rate also exceeds the 62 percent reported for fintech companies on a global scale. Looking ahead, 94 percent of these local firms plan to increase their AI budgets in 2027. However, only 4 percent of the surveyed leaders identify new revenue generation as the primary benefit of the technology.

The Singapore FinTech Association, Airwallex, and Kapronasia were responsible for producing this comprehensive industry report. These organizations highlighted a significant gap between the widespread use of AI and its actual ability to drive business growth. They noted that while the technology is being implemented rapidly, it is not yet translating into substantial new income for most firms. The report suggests that the current focus remains on adoption rather than financial expansion.

Articles.Title: Singapore fintechs lead in AI adoption: survey - Xinhua

stories.Headline: US and China agree to create joint guardrails for superintelligence
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump held a White House news conference on Friday to review his recent trip to Asia. He discussed his productive meeting with President Xi Jinping on Thursday and his arrival at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport on Wednesday afternoon. The visit included the first trilateral summit between the United States, China, and Russia, which took place on Thursday afternoon. This historic meeting occurred on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.

The three leaders issued the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace to prevent nuclear war and reduce nuclear risks. The United States and China also agreed to create joint guardrails for superintelligence to ensure the technology remains under human control. Trump mentioned that he is considering a comprehensive deal with China, though he did not provide specific details regarding chip export restrictions. China's Foreign Ministry stated that both nations will implement an action plan to build a relationship based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity.

President Trump praised his great relationship with President Xi and expressed deep respect for the immaculate development of Shenzhen. He described the city as a clean and flawless modern center that grew from a small fishing village. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that the two leaders agreed humans must always make military decisions rather than allowing AI to act autonomously. President Xi emphasized the need for strong communication and coordination to prevent security risks associated with artificial intelligence.

Articles.Title: Trump reviews Asia trip, praises China ties and discusses joint AI safeguards - China Daily

stories.Headline: Sachin Sharma publishes a Claude bug-hunting skills bundle with 83 skills on GitHub
stories.Summary:
ElementalSoul, also named Sachin Sharma, published the Claude-BugHunter bundle on GitHub, and the explainx.ai article about it is dated 2026-11-15T06:00:00Z. The bundle is a self-contained Agent Skills set that teaches coding agents bug-hunting methodology rather than generic hacker prompts. It ships 83 skills, 15 slash commands, and 681 disclosed-report patterns mapped into 24 vulnerability classes. The repository gained about 124 GitHub stars in a day and sits near 5,900 stars total. The article says agent-assisted offensive security is now default curiosity for Claude Code users, and unauthorized use carries legal and platform-policy risk.

The bundle includes explicit in-scope and out-of-scope lists, and its in-scope list covers web apps, APIs, OAuth, SSRF, IDOR, external M365, Okta, vCenter and VPN chains, and cloud IAM misconfigs. Its out-of-scope list covers internal AD attacks, C2 frameworks, persistence, AMSI bypass, and iOS, kernel and binary pwn. The plugin install runs /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter then /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls, while the copy install uses git clone plus bash scripts/install.sh, with --all for multi-harness. Option A keeps skills namespaced under claude-bughunter: and updates with plugin bumps, and Option B drops files into ~/.claude/skills and enables the hunt engagement scaffolder plus an optional cbh CLI installed with pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter. Multi-harness support copies the same SKILL.md files into Codex, Hermes and Antigravity paths when --all is passed, and slash commands remain Claude-Code-only by design.

The README's Authorization section states the skills target assets you own or have written permission to test and points to triage-validation questions on program scope and accepted impact. The README links the Cyber Verification Program and documents Opus 5 model fallback to Opus 4.8 on some higher-risk cyber classes. For defensive work on code you own, the README suggests framing tasks as remediation reviews such as checking against OWASP Top 10 rather than disguising live offensive engagements to bypass classifiers. The README recommends CVP when the work is genuinely offensive, and it describes a 7-Question Gate covering scope, impact class, reproducibility and related program-policy checks before submission. The README lists DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101 and testphp.vulnweb.com as environments the bundle was exercised against.

The article says BugHunter is not a replacement for human judgment on novel logic bugs and encodes patterns triagers already paid for on public programs. It says the bundle's enterprise skills such as m365-entra-attack, okta-attack, hunt-sharepoint, vmware-vcenter-attack and enterprise-vpn-attack encode 2024 to 2026 CVE chains and appliance quirks for Cisco, Fortinet, Citrix, Palo Alto, Pulse, SonicWall and F5. It says agent-assisted recon can parallelize identity-fabric mapping of Entra and Okta with SSL VPN fingerprinting in one session, and the offensive-osint and web2-recon skills feed a ranked surface list shown in the README quickstart transcript with api.acme.com and GraphQL introspection flagged first. It says evidence-hygiene nudges researchers away from screenshots that leak session cookies or victim PII, and red-team deliverables use redteam-report-template instead of HackerOne markdown. It says bugcrowd-reporting gives VRT-aware severity language, and the article says researchers should keep program rules in a scope.md, run the 7-Question Gate before filing, and redact PII in screenshots.

The article says the bundle's 58 hunt-* skills carry payloads, bypass tables and chain templates derived from disclosed bounty reports, and bb-methodology and redteam-mindset cover non-linear recon, hunt, validate and report flows. It says skills load by topic rather than by name, so a plain-language engagement description pulls the right hunt-* module. It says the engine/ folder maps target surfaces to skills deterministically, and the 15 slash commands include /hunt, /recon and /report. It says eight skills vend from shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty under NOTICE file rules, and the generator public-skills-builder scaffolded the per-class hunt-* skills from disclosed patterns. It says Claude-OSINT is a sister project for recon phases with two skills canonically maintained in BugHunter and re-exported, and installers track manifests and skip duplicate copies.

The README roadmap mentions HackerOne MCP integration, per-engagement memory and quarterly refreshes of enterprise VPN CVE matrices, while Burp MCP is wired today. The article says hunt-fintech-graphql already exists, and healthcare and government compliance hunt skills remain open roadmap entries. It says sponsors ApiSmart and ThreatWatch360 appear in the README footer and do not change the MIT license. It says the README credits Trail of Bits and SecSkills as authoring inspirations without vendoring their trees, and the article recommends reviewing AgentBeam alongside skill installs for defensive agent controls. The article says the README positions the bundle for authorized testing only, and it leaves open whether HackerOne API automation will ship inside the agent.

stories.Headline: Scientists would still find meaning in discovery even if a super intelligence solves all problems
stories.Summary:
Christopher P. Kempes and David C. Krakauer wrote about the future of science on November 19, 2026, for the publication called Nautilus. They explored whether scientists still have roles if a super intelligence reaches a singularity and solves all utilitarian problems at fast rates. The authors compared this potential shift to how astrobiologists would react if an alien species arrived with all known mysteries solved. They argued that human scientists would still find meaning in the craft of discovery even if machines provide the answers. This transition would move the focus of science from producing useful economic solutions to the deeper pursuit of human understanding.

The authors mentioned that Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov in 1997, and AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol in 2016, while AlphaZero learned chess by 2017. They noted that Chess.com grew to over 150 million members and that Sebastian Sawe ran the London Marathon in 1 hour, 59 minutes, 30 seconds. Seiko released the first quartz watch in 1969, which caused a crisis for the Swiss watch industry during the 1970s, but the tourbillon was invented in 1795. Amazon Connect Talent uses a scoring formula from 1 to 5 to evaluate job competencies through structured AI interviews based on industrial-organizational psychology. These AI interviews use job requirements and occupational frameworks to create scorecards that identify specific strength and concern signals for each candidate.

The authors stated that science should focus on the challenge of tool-assisted activities rather than just optimizing tasks for society or economic gain. They suggested that humans might become like philosophers post-science, trying to make sense of other humans and the rest of life in the universe. Ted Chiang observed that we may face a world of hermeneutics where we constantly try to decipher the communications of AI. Geoffrey Hinton, who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, argued for the regulation and slow-down of AI research to ensure safety. He believed that intelligent machines should learn from human behavior bottom-up instead of using top-down definitions and abstractions of analytical reasoning.

Other researchers assume that a super intelligence will rapidly eliminate the need for scientists by solving all the utilitarian problems of the world. The authors noted that the Swiss watch industry survived the quartz crisis by creating more complex mechanical timepieces to demonstrate the watchmaker's skill. They mentioned that physicists once told each other to shut up and calculate to avoid the strangeness of quantum mechanics in their work. Amazon Connect Talent aims to help organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people by providing candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills. This AI service affects hiring teams by separating the interview conversation from the evaluation process to limit the influence of unrelated information.

The articles explain that Frank Rosenblatt pioneered neural networks in 1958, but Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert wrote the book Perceptrons in 1969. This book described neural networks as a sterile direction for applied research, which contributed to an AI winter during the 1970s. Recent AI progress was driven by GPUs for 3D graphics and TPUs derived from Systolic Array technology to minimize memory bottlenecks in computing. These technologies were connected by linear algebra, which provided the necessary matrix multiplications for training new Deep Neural Network architectures in the field. The authors also noted that natural philosophy once separated into natural science and philosophy, similar to the breakup of the Beatles or the Bulls.

Future science may turn its attention to asking what things mean rather than just seeking the next predictive equation or molecular structure. The authors suggest that we must rethink the science of AI because the field currently faces a replication catastrophe in its research. Most current AI methods are custom one-offs applied to proprietary models, which makes many studies unconnected ephemera in a distributed landscape. The articles leave open how we will make meaning among machines and how we will decipher the language of a singularity. It remains unclear how the scientific community will adapt its understanding of how to do science in a world of super intelligence.

stories.Headline: Army works with OpenAI to automate software accreditation for vendors
stories.Summary:
The Army is collaborating with OpenAI to streamline the accreditation process for commercial software vendors seeking to provide products to the military, according to a report by DefenseScoop. The initiative, known as Project Gatekeeper, aims to automate the authority to operate process, which historically takes months to complete. By allowing vendors to submit code to an Army development, security and operations platform for rapid validation, the service intends to lower barriers for industry partners. Acting Army Chief Information Officer Gabe Chiulli stated that the project provides an initial vetting process, granting successful applicants access to secure Army enclaves.

The Army plans to integrate artificial intelligence models into this pipeline within the next quarter, starting with a phased approach using OpenAI tools. This strategy focuses on strategic validation to avoid redundant checks, according to the report. Future phases will likely incorporate additional open source and commercial providers beyond the initial OpenAI tools. To maintain security and privacy, the Army will encourage companies to utilize their own application programming interface keys during the scanning process. This approach ensures that vendors retain control over their vulnerability logs while benefiting from the automated vetting system.

Chiulli said the project offers an initial vetting process that gives successful applicants access to secure Army enclaves, and officials are also working to expand access to the platform beyond current Common Access Card holders by integrating Login.gov. The service intends to lower barriers for industry partners through the rapid validation of submitted code. The phased approach using OpenAI tools is meant to focus on strategic validation and avoid redundant checks. Vendors keep control of their vulnerability logs by using their own application programming interface keys during scanning.

More to follow.

Articles.Title: Army partners with OpenAI to accelerate software accreditation

stories.Headline: Workers AI Superintelligence team releases open-weight Clairic and Clairic-flash models
stories.Summary:
The Workers AI Superintelligence team released updated versions of Clairic and Clairic-flash on November 18, 2026. These two models are now available as open-weight options for users. Cloudflare created these frontier AI models for its customers and the open-source community. The team redesigned the architecture of Clairic after its initial preview release. This update focuses on improving how the model handles unstructured data.

The new Clairic improves extraction from PDFs, images, tables, lists, and dates. Clairic-flash is a compact model with 9 billion parameters for faster performance. Both models are hosted on Workers AI and available on Hugging Face. The updated Clairic uses parallel slot autoregressive generation for text and number fields. This replaces the single forward pass used in the previous preview version.

Alex Reneau, Michelle Chen, and Kevin Flansburg represent the Workers AI Superintelligence team. They stated that Cloudflare has become a neolab for building frontier AI models. The team is working quickly to push the AI frontier for the community. They explained that the redesign makes extraction the clear focus for the model. This allows the model to excel at reading from unstructured data sources.

Customers provided feedback and use cases that influenced the redesign of the model. These users wanted to extract data from support tickets and images like receipts. The open-source community is also affected by the release of these open weights. These groups needed more reliable grounding of answers in the source material. The updates specifically address these needs for better data extraction and prediction.

The team previously announced a preview version of the Clairic extraction model. They also developed another model called Clef before this current release. The company has been building a research team to create useful AI models. This background led to the creation of the Workers AI Superintelligence team. They used customer feedback to go back to the drawing board for Clairic.

The team is currently working on many more models for future release. These new models will continue to serve Cloudflare customers and open-source developers. The articles do not state when the next model will be released. They do not specify the exact size of the full Clairic model. It remains open whether further architectural changes will be made to Clairic-flash.

stories.Headline: Warsh opens Fed task force hearing on AI productivity and jobs
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh started a landmark hearing on Monday, November 16, 2026. He led the first meeting of a task force examining artificial intelligence. The session focused on how this technology could fuel growth or disrupt jobs. Warsh wanted to analyze the impact of AI on US productivity. He warned that overlooking the risks of this technology could be costly.

The Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference took place at the San Francisco Federal Reserve. Warsh established five task forces, including the one that held this first hearing. He assembled Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Microsoft Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. He also included Stanford University professor Charles Jones, who is on leave at Anthropic. These independent heads provide candid feedback to help the Fed set the best policy.

Warsh stated that the widespread adoption of this technology will have a significant economic impact. He said policymakers must be mindful that great opportunities rarely come without some risk. He believes AI, or super intelligence, might differ from past general purpose technologies like electricity. Warsh noted that AI appears to be changing the speed and method of innovation. He argued that broadening idea generation could sustain growth above the long run average.

Warsh asked experts if AI will drive productivity gains and raise general standards of living. He questioned whether the surge will happen sooner in the US or other countries. He wondered if the technology will make achieving price stability harder or easier for policymakers. The hearing aims to determine the implications for jobs in the near and long term. These questions affect the dual mandate of the Federal Reserve regarding the US economy.

Warsh compared AI to the internal combustion engine, noting that previous inventions did not automate ideas. He described a scenario where inflation adjusted GDP growth rises while the US stays employed. He also warned that widespread automation could push the unemployment rate higher by displacing jobs. A third possibility involves a stock market bust if expected returns on AI turn down. This disappointment could lead to an economic slowdown without any lasting productivity gains.

The task force will continue to follow evidence to provide feedback for future monetary policy. Warsh intends to interrogate the reality of the situation by listening to various field experts. The Fed will track the magnitude, scope, and timing of the AI productivity surge. The articles do not state when the next task force hearing will be held. They leave open whether AI will actually increase the long term average of GDP.

Researchers affiliated with ETH Zurich, Blue River Technology, Gravis Robotics and Intel used reinforcement learning and computer simulation to teach a John Deere skid-steer loader to perform autonomous acrobatic manoeuvres. The machine is a 12,000-pound John Deere 332G skid-steer loader, an industrial machine designed primarily for moving materials and performing construction work. The team trained it to lift itself onto two wheels, maintain balance, navigate uneven surfaces and execute controlled spins without assistance. The training relied on reinforcement learning, a machine learning approach in which an artificial agent improves its decisions through rewards and penalties. They first trained the control system inside a simulated environment before transferring its learned instructions to the physical construction machine.

The work changes how such a machine is controlled, because the researchers developed an artificial intelligence system that learned suitable movements through repeated training and feedback instead of relying on conventional programming. The loader can spin while maintaining balance on uneven terrain, and it now balances on two wheels without an operator. The researchers trained the construction machine in simulation before real-world demonstrations, and the machine learned movements normally associated with stunt driving rather than human operators. The demonstrations showed the machine lifting itself onto two wheels, holding its balance and executing controlled spins on its own.

The researchers affiliated with ETH Zurich, Blue River Technology, Gravis Robotics and Intel are responsible for the work, and the articles do not give further statements from them beyond describing the training method and the demonstrations. The articles describe the machine as a John Deere 332G skid-steer loader and say the researchers taught it using reinforcement learning and computer simulation. They report that the control system was trained in a simulated environment first, with the learned instructions then transferred to the physical machine. The articles do not name individual researchers or quote any of them directly.

The context is that the machine is an industrial loader built for moving materials and construction work, and the researchers taught it movements previously associated with highly skilled human operators. stories.Headline: Machine learning and pharmacology screen finds five approved drugs targeting endometrial infertility subtypes
stories.Summary:
A computational framework combining machine learning and systems pharmacology has identified five approved medications capable of targeting distinct molecular abnormalities underlying non-timing endometrial infertility, according to findings published in Reproductive Biology and Endocrinology. The work was reported on November 23, 2026, in an article whose authors include Parraga-Leo, Sebastian-Leon, Sanchez-Reyes, Sanz, Vidal, Sanchez-Ribas, Quiñonero, Wells, Pellicer, Sirota and Diaz-Gimeno. The condition is described as an idiopathic form of endometrial failure that impairs reproductive success during assisted reproduction regardless of embryo quality. The findings offer a targeted strategy to address this non-timing endometrial failure, the article states.

Investigators conducted a multicentre prospective study evaluating 192 endometrial biopsies collected during the mid-secretory phase from female patients undergoing in vitro fertilization. The research team applied machine learning algorithms to transcriptomic data and clinical outcomes to categorize tissue specimens into distinct good-prognosis and poor-prognosis endotypes, which were then partitioned into discrete molecular subendotypes based on shared gene expression alterations and reproductive trajectories. The poor-prognosis endotype, comprising 43 patients, showed a pregnancy rate of 26.3 percent compared to 66.0 percent in the good-prognosis cohort, with a statistically significant difference evaluated at p = 1.99 × 10⁻⁵. Live birth rates were likewise depressed among poor-prognosis patients at 40.0 percent compared to 87.1 percent in good-prognosis controls, at p = 0.0013. The poor-prognosis group also experienced elevated biochemical miscarriage rates of 30.3 percent versus 7.2 percent, at p = 0.0372, alongside heightened clinical miscarriage rates of 42.9 percent versus 6.2 percent, at p = 0.0159.

Deeper algorithmic partitioning divided the poor-prognosis cohort into two distinct molecular subendotypes distinguished by different failure modes and underlying cellular pathology. The first subendotype, encompassing 16 patients, was characterized by an increased biochemical miscarriage rate of 66.7 percent compared to 14.3 percent observed in the alternative poor-prognosis group, at p = 0.0022. The second subendotype, comprising 27 patients, was associated with an elevated clinical miscarriage rate of 50.0 percent compared to 0.0 percent in the first group, at p = 0.0001. In addition to impaired decidualization, the biochemical miscarriage subendotype displayed prominent immune dysregulation, identifying local immune pathway disturbances as a primary biological mechanism contributing to early embryonic loss.

To establish therapeutic countermeasures against these identified transcriptomic dysfunctions, the authors deployed systems pharmacology approaches to evaluate approved pharmaceuticals capable of inverting the abnormal molecular signatures. This in silico screening prioritized five approved compounds possessing target profiles aligned with the dysregulated subendotypes: genistein, pioglitazone, alprostadil, flunisolide and tenoxicam. The therapeutic potential of the computationally selected drugs was subsequently validated through functional biological assays in human endometrial stromal cell lines using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, F-actin cellular staining and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Concurrently, alprostadil, flunisolide and tenoxicam demonstrated clear anti-inflammatory properties by inhibiting well-established biomarkers of endometrial immune response. Although these laboratory observations confirm that repurposed compounds can modulate specific cellular pathways in human endometrial cells, the authors emphasized that formal clinical trials in patient cohorts remain necessary to validate therapeutic efficacy and advance these personalized interventions into routine reproductive medicine.

stories.Headline: Mullin suggests super intelligence may be behind FAA ground stop
stories.Summary:
On November 13, 2026, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop that began at about 3:30 p.m. ET and lasted until air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. ET. The Associated Press called it the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. A little before 5 p.m.

ET, the White House let reporters know that Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin was coming out to talk to them. A reporter asked whether the trouble could be a cyberattack or some kind of AI intrusion. Mullin said, "We don't want to get ahead of ourselves." When the question came up again, Mullin said, "We call it SI around here, remember? SI."

He said, "You just can't rule out anything at this point," and that they were going through that process and would take the appropriate actions. The FAA has spent the fall rolling out a new system for planning air traffic, called SMART, that uses AI. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy unveiled it in September, saying, "We are not outsourcing aviation to AI." On November 10, the FAA expanded SMART nationwide, three days before the ground stop. The FAA says SMART "is a data aggregator, and it does not feed information into the air traffic control system."

Its initial investigation points to two possible sources, in Texas and Arkansas, for the flood of data that made its old equipment unstable. Investigators are examining equipment from both sites, where the FAA's network contractor, L3Harris, had been installing new routers. As of Tuesday, Duffy said they still didn't have "clarity" on the root cause. SMART's developer, Air Space Intelligence, has denied any role for "the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC." On Monday night, Mullin went on Fox News, where Sean Hannity asked him whether the ground stop and the outages at Microsoft, United and a couple of big banks were connected.

Mullin said he doesn't always believe in coincidences until he's proven wrong, and that CISA said it was not seeing any traffic that would make it think this was a cyberattack. He said a tech figure who asked not to be named, and who was not Elon, told him, "I believe that it's the SI." Mullin said he could tell Hannity with 98% certainty, "we're not seeing the cyberattack." Politico reported Wednesday that after the interview, "Trump administration group chats lit up with 'WTFs,'" according to a person close to the White House. That afternoon, at a House Homeland Security Committee hearing, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, the guy Trump picked to run his new "Super Intelligence Force," called the recent outages "separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes."

On September 19, Trump wrote on Truth Social that "Many people think that the words 'Artificial Intelligence' are inaccurate, and very ineloquent," and offered three replacements: "Superior Intelligence (SI) or, Extreme Intelligence (EI) or, Supreme Intelligence (SI)." When YouGov asked which name was better, 53% of Americans picked "artificial intelligence" and 9% picked "super intelligence." Standing in front of the United Nations General Assembly, Trump announced that "the use of the word 'artificial' makes intelligence fake." He then issued an executive order to make it official, that "to the maximum extent permitted by law, the executive branch shall use the terms 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI' in place of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI.'"

On Truth Social, he declared that "The White House considers anyone that uses the term, 'Artificial Intelligence,' as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, 'Super Intelligence,' THE ENEMY!" Trump's first-day executive order made the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America" as far as the federal government is concerned, and when AP style kept calling it the Gulf of Mexico, the White House barred AP reporters from the Oval Office and Air Force One. In August, in the middle of a trade fight with Canada, Trump ordered the government to start calling Lake Ontario "Lake America." More to follow.

stories.Headline: Experts doubt AI superintelligence warnings from Amodei and Altman
stories.Summary:
In a column published by the Orange County Register on November 16, 2026, columnist Rafael Perez examined warnings from AI industry leaders about superintelligence and asked experts whether those fears are justified. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that within the next year AI may cripple the internet and cause billions of dollars in damage, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told the United Nations Security Council that humanity could lose control of the future to AI. Researchers at Anthropic warned that AI could lead to human extinction, and one of them, Jacob Coxon, quit in protest, saying developers are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with lives. The fears center on recursive self-improvement, the idea that models could iteratively improve themselves far faster than people can improve them, possibly producing an intelligence explosion and a superintelligence that would be virtually impossible to control.

The experts Perez consulted were deeply skeptical that this is where the field is heading. Dr. Melanie Mitchell, an AI and cognitive science researcher and professor at the Santa Fe Institute, said she does not think agents are anywhere close to improving themselves so vastly, and that while systems can generate code and use it to improve the code behind AI systems, the result is a very gradual thing rather than an exponential runaway. Dr. Luciano Floridi, a philosopher of AI, founding director of the Digital Ethics Center at Yale University and an advisor to the European Union on AI policy, said nobody has shown that the field is on the way to recursive self-improvement, comparing the claim to a train from New Haven to New York that goes fast but never gets closer to Boston. He said the intelligence explosion imagined by I. J. Good in the 1960s remains a logical, sci-fi possibility with no demonstrated route to it, and both experts noted that software has improved software for decades, as a compiler does, and that existing models help build the next ones in laboratories, which speeds up work without removing the hands that decide what counts as an improvement.

Floridi pointed to a persistent problem: AI research requires judgment about whether a modification is an improvement, and models have not shown competence at that, which the column describes as only the tip of the engineering challenge. Perez also asked why someone would quit a comfortable job at a leading AI lab if the warned threat were not legitimate, and he offered performative moral grandstanding as one suggested possibility while proposing a less vicious explanation, that the field is extremely difficult to evaluate even for experts. Mitchell said the field is quite polarized, with many people agreeing with her and many heatedly disagreeing, and that the fighting reflects general uncertainty. Perez concluded that if these experts are correct there is little reason to worry about an existential threat from superintelligence, and that acknowledging this matters because hysteria over AI diverts attention from the very real problems AI is creating in society, which he said an upcoming column would address.

stories.Headline: FDA launches Super Intelligence hub to detail its AI governance and regulatory use
stories.Summary:
The Food and Drug Administration has launched a new Super Intelligence web hub that brings together information on the agency's use of artificial intelligence, its internal governance, and its regulatory activities involving AI-enabled technologies. The hub outlines how the FDA uses AI tools to support scientific reviews, inspections, investigations, and other regulatory functions. The agency states that authorized tools must meet applicable federal security requirements and that agency personnel remain responsible for regulatory decisions. The launch follows several earlier FDA modernization efforts, including the May 2026 release of Elsa 4.0 and the consolidation of more than 40 application and submission data sources, systems, and portals into HALO, its Harmonized AI & Lifecycle Operations for Data platform.

The hub identifies two councils responsible for coordinating the agency's AI activities, with the External Policy council handling policy development, regulatory strategy, and stakeholder engagement across FDA centers and offices. The Internal Operations council oversees internal AI governance and provides guidance and support for agency tools, capabilities, and initiatives in coordination with federal and HHS partners. The FDA also began integrating Elsa 4.0 and HALO to allow employees to query agency data and build workflows without manually uploading documents into individual chats. The new hub provides links to AI-related resources across the agency's drug, biologics, medical device, oncology, tobacco, and food programs, along with the 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory.

The FDA's technology efforts are led by Jared Seehafer, Deputy Commissioner for Technology and Chief Super Intelligence Officer, whose responsibilities include agencywide strategy for technology, software, data, and SI. The agency states that authorized tools must meet applicable federal security requirements and that personnel remain responsible for regulatory decisions. These activities align with the FDA's Public Health Pillars, which identify AI regulatory frameworks, digital health, scientific tools, and modernization of agencywide systems and digital infrastructure among the agency's priorities. The launch does not announce new contracting requirements, funding commitments, or acquisition timelines.

For companies tracking FDA technology priorities, the hub and its associated resources provide a consolidated starting point for reviewing the agency's existing AI activities. stories.Headline: NTT presents photonics, optical quantum computing and space plans at R&D Forum 2026
stories.Summary:
NTT held its R&D Forum 2026 this week, with president and CEO Akira Shimada and senior vice president Shingo Kinoshita leading a private press conference through the company's latest core developments in photonics, optical quantum computing, AI and space. The company presented its IOWN initiative, its vision for an ultra-high-capacity, ultra-low-latency and ultra-low-power network that it says is now aligned for AI and designed to meet the demands of the AI era. NTT also set out its push into space computing under the NTT C89 brand, a name chosen because there are 88 officially recognised constellations in the night sky, signalling its ambition to link its space businesses, services and R&D into a new 89th constellation. The company said it is looking at lunar surface communication and lunar energy transmission. NTT co-founded the IOWN Global Forum in 2020 with Intel and Sony, and the non-profit organisation now has more than 170 members.

Shimada said satellite connectivity will expand beyond vehicles to ships, buildings and other critical infrastructure, and that satellite data volumes are exploding, with 230 petabytes per day anticipated by 2033, which is why NTT will turn to light to move data satellite-to-satellite and satellite-to-ground with more capacity and low latency. NTT is working to connect a datacentre in space and to create Earth-Moon communication over the 380,000 kilometres between the planet and the Moon, and Shimada said NTT will where necessary enable AI processing of data in space before returning it to Earth, which he said will prove invaluable in areas such as tracking natural disasters. NTT C89 has signed a memorandum of understanding with Ireland's MBRYONICS to build space optical transceivers, and in September 2026 it reached an agreement with France's Cailabs to link optical ground stations to NTT's All-Photonics Network and datacentres. Minako Tsumenaga, senior vice president and head of the alliance division in research and development marketing at NTT, said the company aims to extend the communication and digital infrastructure it has cultivated on the ground into space, realising a new social infrastructure that seamlessly integrates space and Earth, and that NTT will work to realise a communication and data distribution platform linking satellites and the ground. Shimada said NTT's AI work is shared across three focus areas: infrastructure through IOWN and a distributed datacentre strategy, models including its compact in-house Japanese LLM tsuzumi that runs on a single GPU on-premises or in a private cloud, and sovereign AI for governments and enterprises that need data kept under their own control.

On quantum computing, NTT is developing a photonics-based quantum computer alongside the startup OptQC, targeting a fault-tolerant, million-qubit-class machine by FY2030, and it says optical technologies help solve two major obstacles to a large-scale quantum computer, namely power and cooling. The forum also covered autonomous mobility and AIOWN, an AI-native infrastructure built to support every type of AI, with live demonstrations of photonics-electronics convergence for ultra-low power consumption, AI orchestration technologies that maximise token-processing efficiency through intelligent traffic control, and advanced optimisation of computing resources. NTT is also exploring AI-native network operations without human intervention, including AI agents that automatically generate and verify network infrastructure operation scenarios, traffic monitoring technology that reduces the effort of searching for anomaly analysis, and multi-AI agents that achieve autonomous recovery from network failures and autonomous learning of recovery strategies. The article ends mid-sentence as it moves into quantum-related research on hardware and software evolution, and it gives no further details on what happens next.

New Forge and Omni offerings, described as AI software as a service for production and cloud as a service respectively, are said to broaden enterprise monetization opportunities while mitigating customer concentration risks. stories.Summary:
Matt Stoller reported on an ongoing artificial intelligence crash on November 23, 2026. This financial downturn followed the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang several weeks prior. The crash also involved a failed initial public offering for the company Anthropic. On Friday, the NASDAQ fell by more than five percent into a correction. Other markets and commodities also dropped during this period of volatility.

The crash involves Nvidia losing three trillion dollars in market value. Neocloud stock prices fell by more than half, and their debt reached junk levels. Oracle reached a 52-week low and issued a denial of insolvency on November 20, 2026. This company claimed it secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. The 10-year Treasury bond rose from 4 percent in February to 5.27 percent.

Matt Stoller claims the AI trade is over and financial systems may blow up. He suggests the market is likely in a bear market rather than a temporary pullback. Stoller believes Nvidia's board may have fired Jensen Huang for committing fraud. He argues that the company claimed chip sales that were not actually happening. He notes that the current crash is prompted by high borrowing costs.

Steve Eisman claims that many medium-sized AI companies known as neoclouds are going to zero. Michael Burry has reportedly made similar statements about the AI trade. Senator Adam Schiff wrote in the Wall Street Journal that there will be no bailout. Hedge funds like Situational Awareness were affected, selling portfolios in July. The crash affects superrich managers, Wall Street bankers, and Silicon Valley monopolists.

The bubble grew as corporations used financial models that did not cover debt service costs. Leverage in the hedge fund sector increased after the Silicon Valley Bank bailout. The gross asset value of hedge funds reached 13 trillion dollars against 4 trillion net. This leverage grew since late 2022 and early 2023 when ChatGPT launched. Borrowing costs rose due to the war in Iran and Federal Reserve rate hikes.

The market may experience a bear market bounce before resuming its slide. Stoller suggests the Federal Reserve would need radical action to prevent a bear market. stories.Headline: Hyderabad municipal corporation commissions Osmania University to draft AI traffic management plan for 429 signals
stories.Summary:
The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation has begun work on an artificial intelligence-powered traffic management system covering 429 traffic signal locations across the Greater Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri municipal corporations, according to The New Indian Express. The corporation has entrusted the Department of Electrical Engineering at the University College of Engineering, Osmania University, with preparing the Detailed Project Report for the project. The GHMC Standing Committee has approved 2.83 crore rupees for the purpose, the newspaper reported on 23 November 2026. The proposed system, called CURE-ITMS, will integrate all 429 signal locations within the CURE limits on a common AI-enabled platform, with plans to extend the network beyond the Outer Ring Road.

The system is expected to regulate traffic dynamically based on real-time conditions, improve traffic flow during peak hours and heavy rainfall, facilitate the movement of emergency vehicles and enhance road safety. It is also aimed at replacing the fragmented approach to traffic signal maintenance and regulation with an integrated, technology-driven network. GHMC officials said that at recent review meetings chaired by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and the MAUD Special Chief Secretary, officials were directed to modernise all 429 signalised junctions within CURE limits and extend the network beyond the Outer Ring Road. The directions also included developing an Integrated Traffic Data Platform, identifying accident-prone locations and emergency vehicle routes, and testing AI-based traffic management technologies through pilot projects.

The state government has also proposed setting up a dedicated institutional mechanism, Traffic Management and Road Safety, known as TG-TMARS, to oversee traffic management and road safety initiatives. The government has already accorded administrative sanction of 77.31 crore rupees for maintaining existing traffic signals, upgrading and rewiring old ones, and installing and maintaining 50 new traffic signals and 15 Pelican signals. The latest proposal envisages a broader approach, covering the operation and maintenance of existing signals across CURE limits, installation of additional signals and AI-based road safety measures, including traffic signage and allied infrastructure. Identification and installation of additional signals are planned for December 2026.

The Osmania University team has been given four weeks to prepare the DPR, detailing the technological requirements, implementation framework and other aspects of the project. The proposed AI-based traffic regulation and road safety technologies will initially be tested through pilot projects before wider implementation, according to the report.

stories.Headline: Nscale suspends hiring across several divisions to cut costs ahead of a potential $35bn flotation
stories.Summary:
The British artificial intelligence company Nscale halted recruitment in several divisions on November 21, 2026, to reduce costs. This decision follows a period of rapid growth and comes as the firm prepares for a potential $35bn flotation on the New York Stock Exchange. The company has seen its workforce expand from 300 employees earlier this year to more than 1,100 people. This move occurs amid a broader market sell-off and rising borrowing costs for data centre operators.

The cost-cutting drive requires executives to suspend hiring for a few months, except for critical roles, and reduce discretionary spending. Nscale, which was founded two years ago by former cryptocurrency executive Josh Payne, has raised over $13bn and signed deals with Microsoft and Anthropic. The company reported a loss of $1.7bn during the first nine months of this year on revenues of $308m. Additionally, Nscale lost a $3.2bn Microsoft deal due to delays in securing a grid connection.

Chief operating officer Justin Osofsky, who previously worked at Meta, told staff that the business needs time to catch up with its growth. He explained that financing large projects is taking longer across the sector, making careful cash management essential for future opportunities. Osofsky stated that preserving every dollar provides the company with more flexibility to fund its highest priority projects. He emphasized that the firm must hold itself to a higher bar regarding its spending.

The company faces a difficult environment following the departure of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and anti-data centre victories in the US Midterms. Nscale also warned Norwegian officials that its expansion plans could fall apart due to a moratorium on new data centres. In a letter dated November 1, the firm requested an urgent meeting with Norway's energy ministry. Ministers subsequently blocked new grid connections and technical approvals for data centres until next August.

stories.Headline: Brampton students pitch AI fixes for local businesses at first hackathon
stories.Summary:
The Brampton Venture Zone held its first student hackathon over the weekend of November 21 and 22, 2026, according to CBC News. The event, called the Brampton AI Innovator Hackathon, took place at the Brampton Venture Zone, an incubator run with Toronto Metropolitan University. It was the first stage of a year-long program that will partner post-secondary students with Brampton-based businesses to use artificial intelligence to address day-to-day challenges. About 120 students worked in groups of three to four over the two days on challenges from 13 participating Brampton businesses. The businesses want to adapt to AI but lack the teams or resources to do it, said Dione Almedia, the lead of marketing and partnerships for the Venture Zone.

Students worked with mentors, judges and the businesses that supplied the challenges so they could understand each problem and how to solve it, Almedia said. Bilawal Bhullar, the CEO and founder of Sigma Security Services, one of the participating businesses, asked students to draft solutions to last-minute customer requests, such as a jump in the number of security personnel needed for an event. He said this is a frequent problem in his industry and that it is important for business owners to empower the next generation with opportunities to learn about the real world outside the classroom. About a third of the participating students were selected as finalists. Those finalists will compete to work with the 13 local businesses in the first eight months of 2027 to develop their pitches into solutions.

Tomi Tijani was selected as a finalist alongside his teammates Shayan Khan, Ibrahim Mohamud and Isaiah Ozekhome, and their pitch focused on pharmacology. Tijani said the team wanted to show that the health sector is not something that can be played with and how AI can make it a better place. He said the hackathon gave him a chance to demonstrate his knowledge and skillset and to network with industry professionals. He said his LinkedIn connections rose from about 250 to 373 and that he worked not just with his team but with business professionals and entrepreneurs. The article gives no further details on what happens after the finalists work with the businesses in 2027.

stories.Headline: Deloitte and Workday host a Central Europe webinar on people and AI as a competitive advantage
stories.Summary:
Deloitte and Workday are holding a webinar for Central Europe on the theme of people and AI as a competitive advantage, exploring the findings of Deloitte’s 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report and what those findings mean for enterprise transformation. The session is aimed at CHROs and HR leaders across Central Europe and is designed to connect human capital trends with the decisions shaping AI-enabled organisations. According to the announcement, 70% of business leaders identify being “fast and nimble” as their primary competitive strategy for the next three years, and the session will examine how organisations can rethink work to keep pace with AI. Leaders and experts from Workday and Deloitte will explore the shift from “Humans + Machines” to “Humans x Machines,” combining human judgement with machine speed to create greater value. The announcement says the session will also examine what this “Human Advantage” means for HR and how it can inform the way organisations approach AI-enabled transformation.

The webinar focuses on three priorities for HR leaders trying to bridge the gap between understanding these trends and putting them into practice. The first is creating value through people and AI, moving beyond cost efficiency to explore how people and AI can work together to deliver greater business value. The second is adapting workforce planning, including understanding the “Orchestration Advantage” and the shift from static plans to dynamically aligning capabilities and capacity with business needs. The third is navigating cultural change, exploring how AI is reshaping organisational culture, what “Cultural Debt” means and how to manage its ripple effects. The announcement invites people to register to explore how to move beyond experimentation and take a more strategic approach to people, work and AI.

The articles do not name the individual leaders and experts from Workday and Deloitte who will take part, and they give no date or time for the session beyond the publication date of the announcement, 19 November 2026. No specific statements from named people are included, so responsibility for the views rests with the two firms as organisers rather than with any quoted individual. The context given is Deloitte’s 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report and the finding that 70% of business leaders see being “fast and nimble” as their primary competitive strategy for the next three years. Camtek had recently reported Q3 2026 revenue that was 28% higher than a year earlier. Management guidance points to about US$180 million in Q4 sales and a 2027 revenue outlook above US$800 million. The upgrade ties Camtek's tools directly to capacity plans in AI focused advanced packaging rather than to broad semiconductor spending.

The 2027 outlook above US$800 million sits on top of more than US$600 million of 2026 year to date orders, roughly 80% tied to AI and HBM. Those orders are scheduled into 2026 and 2027, and capacity is rising toward well over US$700 million of annual revenue. Camtek is scaling new German manufacturing capacity while lifting gross margin toward the 52.5% to 53% range and operating margin toward 30% to 32% by late 2026. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St holds that Camtek's Hawk and Eagle G5 tools are already central to customer roadmaps.

stories.Headline: IndexBox forecasts growth for thin wafer processing and dicing equipment through 2035
stories.Summary:
IndexBox released a market report on November 21, 2026, regarding thin wafer processing and dicing equipment. This global market is entering a structural growth phase driven by advanced semiconductor packaging demand. The report provides a comprehensive analysis of the industry from 2026 through 2035. It highlights a shift toward thinner wafers and higher die density for heterogeneous integration. This equipment is now a critical enabler for 3D IC stacking and chiplet designs.

The baseline scenario projects a compound annual growth rate of 6.8 percent from 2026 to 2035. The market index is projected to reach 185 by 2035, using 2025 as a base of 100. Advanced packaging represents 35 percent of demand, while power semiconductors account for 25 percent. Memory and logic devices hold 20 percent, and MEMS and sensors represent 12 percent. Wafers for advanced packaging must be thinned to below 50 micrometers.

IndexBox states that the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals and more disciplined procurement behavior. They note that the supply architecture is now more regionally diversified than it was previously. The report claims that the transition to laser and plasma singulation is accelerating to process brittle materials. These technologies are necessary to achieve near-zero kerf loss for silicon carbide and gallium nitride. The analysts suggest that long-term trajectories remain positive despite some cyclical semiconductor spending.

The report identifies Applied Materials, DISCO Corporation, EV Group, SUSS MicroTec, and Tokyo Electron as representative participants. Other key players include Lam Research, ASM International, Plasma-Therm, and Advanced Dicing Technologies. Electric vehicle manufacturers and 5G infrastructure providers are affected by these technological shifts. High-performance computing and mobile applications also drive the need for fan-out wafer-level packaging. These sectors require precise, damage-free singulation that traditional mechanical blade dicing cannot deliver.

The background includes a shift toward wide-bandgap semiconductors like silicon carbide for use in electric vehicles. Eurostat data shows producer unit values for semiconductor manufacture machines were 666,667.00 EUR per piece in 2025. European Union industry output for other special-purpose machinery rose 35.6 percent year-on-year in August 2026. Producer prices for that same machinery category rose 1.5 percent year-on-year in September 2026. Asia-Pacific is the dominant hub for production, while North America and Europe lead system design.

Future growth depends on the ramp-up of AI accelerators and high-bandwidth memory through 2035. The market must overcome high capital costs and qualification cycles that can exceed 18 months. Geopolitical trade tensions and export controls remain potential constraints on equipment sales to certain regions. Technical challenges include managing breakage and thermal issues when processing ultra-thin wafers. The report leaves open how alternative packaging approaches might reduce the need for dicing.

stories.Headline: Investors dump semiconductor stocks amid concerns over an artificial intelligence bubble
stories.Summary:
Investors dumped semiconductor stocks on the New York Stock Exchange over the weekend due to continued vigilance regarding an artificial intelligence bubble. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 10.73 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite returned all of its gains for this year. On November 20, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 48,147.33, which was a decline of 1.93 percent. The S&P 500 fell 3.70 percent to 6910.39, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28 percent to 22,617.73. The volatility index rose 26.20 percent to close at 35.89, marking the highest level since April 2025.

The S&P 500 fell for seven consecutive trading days, which was the longest decline since February 2020. The Dow Jones and S&P 500 entered a correction phase by falling more than 10 percent from previous highs. Nvidia shares fell 14.01 percent, and Micron shares fell 13.89 percent on the New York Stock Exchange. Three-month futures for electric copper on the London Metal Exchange closed at 12,160 dollars per ton on November 20. This copper price represents a 2.92 percent drop from the previous day and a 13.37 percent fall since November 4.

Seo Sang-young of Mirae Asset Securities said the high corporate value of the AI industry became a burden. He noted that Antropics fell after a public offering and AMD reported short selling in China. He also mentioned a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accounting survey of Nvidia as a factor. Kim Sung-no of BNK Investment & Securities said the Antropic listing and Nvidia issues caused the sharp decline. He stated that selling other stocks to buy new listings shows that U.S. market liquidity is not as good as before.

Analysts say the domestic stock market will likely start with a sharp decline on Monday, November 23. This potential Black Monday is influenced by the strong selling of foreigners in the Korean market. From November 16 to 20, foreigners sold a net 4.5159 trillion won in the regular and aftermarket. Institutions also sold 454.7 billion won during this same period. Foreigners specifically targeted Samsung Electronics with 1.79 trillion won in net selling and SK Hynix with 94.1 billion won.

The market plunge happened because AI-related market sentiment instability did not subside rather than from new bad news. Hedge sales related to options contributed to the plunge because November option expiration dates overlapped on November 20. Copper prices fell because of concerns that AI data center projects will be delayed after U.S. midterm elections. The "Blue Wave" in the U.S. midterm elections is analyzed as a factor in the copper price decline. Copper is used in power generation, transmission, and use, and is used in large quantities for AI data centers.

Foreign selling is expected to continue in the Korean market for the time being due to deteriorated liquidity. The domestic stock market faces a burden as major indexes and indicators plunge. The articles leave open whether the AI bubble vigilance will lead to further semiconductor stock dumps. It remains unclear if the S&P 500 will continue its decline beyond the seven consecutive days. stories.Headline: Bill Kinison partners with Uare.AI to revive comic Sam Kinison through artificial intelligence
stories.Summary:
Bill Kinison, the brother and former manager of the comedian Sam Kinison, is partnering with the AI firm Uare.AI to revive the shrieking comic through artificial intelligence, according to a report published by Kotaku on November 22, 2026. Sam Kinison, a Pentecostal preacher turned comic, was part of the 1980s wave of Comedy Store stand-ups and became a pop culture fixture through his signature screaming style. He hosted Saturday Night Live, appeared in Rodney Dangerfield’s Back to School and played Lee Arenberg’s conscience in an episode of Tales from the Crypt. He died at only 38 in 1992 when a drunk driver collided into him with a pickup truck.

The venture pairs Bill Kinison with Uare.AI, a firm founded in 2024 that focuses on training its models on specific voices and personalities rather than broader compilations of stolen data. Talent agency Buchwald says the venture will expand opportunities for Kinison across multiple verticals. In a statement provided to Variety, Bill Kinison said Sam was always on the cutting-edge of comedy and entertainment, and that the genius of Uare.ai’s work and the Buchwald agency’s vision were keeping the promise of his brother’s legacy alive. He added that he could not wait to see what Sam will do.

Bill Kinison and Buchwald are the parties responsible for the venture, and the statement paraphrased above is what Bill Kinison said about it. The Kotaku report notes that the living Kinison was known to pass up on selling his image, snapping a contract with Slim Jim that instead went to Macho Man Randy Savage. It also places the deal in a wider context, noting that while many living celebrities are trying to hedge against this exact scenario, the estates of deceased stars have begun pawning their images. In May, ElevenLabs announced that it would be replicating the uncanny voice and likeness of Stan Lee to say excelsior in audiobooks, and Gene Wilder’s estate is leasing his ghost for a Netflix reality show based around Willy Wonka.

The articles do not say what form the Kinison revival will take, when it will launch or what it will cost, and they give no further details on what happens next beyond the partnership and the statements above.

All 16 Intelligent Eyewear models listed on Gentle Monster’s official website are marked as pre-order sold out, and pre-orders underway in the United States are also understood to have sold out across all models. The glasses bring Google’s latest AI model, Gemini, into a lightweight frame of about 41g that includes a built-in camera, speaker and microphone.

Users can carry out a range of AI functions through voice commands alone without taking their smartphones out of their pockets, and the product focuses on everyday convenience. It offers services including real-time foreign language translation, directions to a destination and summaries of complex meeting materials, and it was designed to let people make natural use of AI in the ordinary setting of wearing glasses. Samsung will officially launch the product in the Korean and U.S. markets on Dec. 10 and begin full-scale sales. In Korea it will first introduce the 16 designs developed with Gentle Monster, while in the U.S. it plans a total lineup of 30 models by adding 14 products from the local brand Warby Parker.

stories.Headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says the company limits product release speed despite capability
stories.Summary:
Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei appeared alongside board members during the company's IPO at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York on Nov. 19, according to American Banker. Dario Amodei, the CEO of the newly public Anthropic, said something extraordinary the other day, the publication reported. In explaining what he calls pacing in terms of developing the company's products, he used the metaphor of a car that could drive 200 miles an hour. He said the company could drive at 200 miles an hour but maybe should only drive at 90 miles an hour. Amodei was presenting this as an example of the elevated reasoning at the company.

In other words, the company could develop its products at break-neck speed and release them, but Anthropic has chosen not to do that, according to the account. The article, published by American Banker on Nov. 23, 2026, carries the headline that Anthropic's business model is creating a new kind of debt, called comprehension debt. The piece was written by Paul Vigna, the managing editor of American Banker, who is described as an author, journalist, editor and speaker with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. The article presents Amodei's pacing remark as an illustration of the reasoning he says the company applies.

The account attributes the pacing explanation and the car metaphor directly to Amodei, the chief executive of the company. It describes the remark as extraordinary and frames the choice to hold back on speed as an example of elevated reasoning at the company. The article does not elaborate further on what comprehension debt means or how it would work. No other named person is quoted in the piece on this point.

The article appears in American Banker's artificial intelligence coverage, dated Nov. 23, 2026, and was posted under the bank notes and cyber security sections of the site. The publication's page also lists other items, including a piece on patchmageddon and recent tech outages that references Anthropic's Claude Mythos model. The article does not say what happens next with the pacing approach or the debt it describes. More to follow.

stories.Headline: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes industry limits on powerful AI models
stories.Summary:
OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed that AI developers adopt common limits on increasingly powerful models and use perplexity as a shared metric for measuring AI progress across the industry, according to a proposal reported by Reuters on Sunday, November 22, 2026. In the proposal, Pachocki wrote that developers should commit to not crossing common limits based on perplexity and other measurements until the industry's ability to understand and monitor AI behaviour reaches a certain concrete milestone. He described perplexity as a model intelligence metric that measures how well a model predicts the next token, the basic unit of data, on average, and he wrote that lower perplexity means better predictions. Pachocki said AI could help drive fundamental advances in AI training methods as soon as 2027, which could accelerate progress faster than advances in monitoring and safety.

The proposal calls for an industry standard that sets a first limit on development and defines which milestones must be met before that limit is exceeded, and it asks developers to hold to agreed capability thresholds until new monitoring and safety mechanisms are in place. Pachocki framed the plan around safety and control, writing that the limits would stay in force until the ability to understand and monitor AI behaviour reaches the concrete milestone he described. The article gives no further numbers, dates or named thresholds beyond the 2027 reference and the perplexity metric itself. The proposal was unveiled amid growing concern inside and outside the industry about the potential risks of AI's rapidly growing capabilities.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman backed the proposal, saying in a post on X that the industry should seek agreement on common limits for AI development, and he described Pachocki's essay as the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while. Altman said such limits would help ensure safety and control. The article attributes the proposal to Pachocki and the backing to Altman, and it names no other companies, regulators or governments involved in the effort. The article does not say what specific limits would be set, who would enforce them, or when any agreement might be reached.

The article places the proposal against warnings that rapid advances could outpace critical safety safeguards, and it notes concern about AI risks both inside and outside the industry. It reports Pachocki's view that AI could speed up advances in AI training methods as soon as 2027, potentially faster than monitoring and safety can keep up. Beyond the call for industry agreement and the 2027 reference, the articles give no timeline for adoption, no details of any forthcoming meeting, and no response from other developers or regulators. More to follow.
