stories.Headline: Harvard's Yu presents CHIEF pathology AI model for bladder cancer analysis
stories.Summary:
Kun-Hsing Yu, an associate professor at Harvard Medical School, discussed foundation AI models for pathology image analysis in bladder cancer at the BCAN Think Tank annual meeting, in a UroToday video posted on November 22, 2026. He described his lab's CHIEF model, which was trained on more than 15 million pathology image patches plus an additional 60,000 hosted images from 19 different anatomical sites. The model aligns image findings with text annotations from pathology reports using the CLIP method first proposed by OpenAI. Yu said the model was evaluated for making cancer diagnosis, predicting molecular profiles and survival prediction. He spoke with Ashish Kamat, a urologic oncologist in Houston, Texas, and a professor of urology at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center.

Yu said a foundation model is a large general-purpose machine learning model trained on broad and diverse data that can be adopted to a wide range of downstream tasks. He cited GPT, Gemini and Claude as families of foundation models developed using vast amounts of human-generated text and image. He said the CHIEF model extracts detailed features from individual image regions and aggregates them into a patient-level representation to capture simple-level patterns. He said several related models using similar approaches have appeared since CHIEF's publication, each with different training data, architectures and combinations of image and language information. He said imaging-based models capture only one dimension of a patient's disease, and that pathology slides, radiology scans, genomic and transcriptomic profiles, medical records, treatment regimen and family history are among the data included in multimodal models.

Yu argued that true clinical impact requires integrating pathology with radiology, genomic, transcriptomic and clinical record data into multimodal models rather than imaging alone. He said this multimodal framework enables discovery of new biomarkers, improves patient prediction and supports translation of insights into clinical care. In bladder cancer specifically, he said this means more accurate risk stratification, better prediction of recurrence and treatment response, and more personalized treatment selection. He said clinical deployment must minimize clicks and cognitive burden rather than add them, and should make clear when a clinician is expected to act on the output or override it. He said accountability requires defining who owns the final clinical decision and monitoring performance shift and unintended harms vigorously after deployment, with a clear process for escalation and correction.

Yu said clinical trust comes from transparency, and that models must communicate the basis and limits of their output and make uncertainty visible to end users while preserving meaningful human oversight. He said responsibility has to be built into the entire AI system, not only added to the end. He predicted pathologists will not be replaced by AI, but that those who adopt it will replace those who don't. He closed by paraphrasing John F. Kennedy, saying we should ask not what AI can do for you but what we can do together to build a better future with AI in medicine.

Kamat said AI and machine learning have seen an explosion in medicine, and noted that niche companies such as Valar Labs have developed AI algorithms that look at tissue and are trained on large data sets as closed platforms. Kamat asked whether pathology AI will remain restricted to certain proprietary platforms or become a general pathology AI available across the globe in the near future. Yu agreed it was a great question and observation, and began to note that several proprietary platforms currently exist. The discussion was part of a breakout session at this year's BCAN Think Tank annual meeting on how AI is beginning to read risk directly from tissue.

Yu's biography lists him as an associate professor in the Department of Biomedical Informatics at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts. Kamat's biography lists him as a professor of urology and the Wayne B. Duddleston Professor of Cancer Research at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, Texas. Related content listed with the video includes BCANTT 2026: AI in Bladder Cancer: What's Real, What's Next, and What to Watch Out For, and sessions on artificial intelligence and machine learning in bladder cancer pathology and clinical decision-making with Hikmat Al-Ahmadie and Alexandre Zlotta. Another related item is Harnessing Artificial Intelligence in Bladder Cancer: Digital Tools for Enhanced Diagnosis and Treatment with David McConkey.

The article was published on UroToday's Bladder Cancer Center of Excellence page, dated November 22, 2026, and the video was posted on November 21, 2026. The page carries a cookie notice with a privacy policy and an I Agree button. The transcript ends mid-sentence as Yu was describing proprietary platforms. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI stock volatility triggers market declines and regulatory interventions in Asia
stories.Summary:
US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, November 23, 2026, while Asian markets declined. This volatility followed a severe wipeout of technology and chip stocks linked to the artificial intelligence boom during the previous week. The downturn was triggered by the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a weak debut for the company Anthropic. Investors are now questioning if the massive borrowed funds used for AI data centers will generate sufficient returns.

The Nasdaq experienced a 10 percent drop last week, marking its largest weekly decline since March 2020. Taiwanese shares fell 17 percent for the week, which was their biggest weekly drop since 1990, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 10 percent on Friday. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures rose nearly 3 percent and S&P 500 futures increased by 2 percent. Meanwhile, South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 3 percent, and Anthropic closed 8.5 percent lower on its first full trading day.

Various regional authorities are now implementing support measures to stabilize their respective financial markets. Taiwan's financial regulator ordered a tightening of short-selling rules on Saturday, and Chinese stock exchanges eased requirements for margin financing. The South Korean finance ministry stated on Sunday that it would deploy market stabilization funds immediately if the benchmark index continued to fall. These actions follow a period where the benchmark index in South Korea slumped to 10-month lows.

The broader AI trade had previously boosted a wide range of stocks, including electricity generators and cable makers. However, these shares have faced pressure in recent months due to rising interest rates. Market participants are now monitoring whether the current recovery in US futures can offset the selling pressure seen in Japan and Hong Kong. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Etsy sellers in Canada pull products as Etsy adds AI training to its terms
stories.Summary:
Some Etsy sellers across Canada are removing their products from the platform after the company added language about artificial intelligence model training to its updated terms and agreements. Tsuki Matsuba, a Vancouver-based seller of custom stationery, is pulling her products from Etsy ahead of the new policy, which the company is rolling out next month. Matsuba told CBC News that the change felt like a kick in the teeth for sellers like her. The update to the company's terms and agreements takes effect on Dec. 16 and includes a line allowing Etsy, its third party partners and vendors to use sellers' content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.

The policy change requires sellers who remain on the platform to accept that their content may be used for AI training, and some shop owners are responding by removing their products and original artwork. Artist Tina Nawrocki, who is based in Ottawa, wrote on X that she is closing down her Etsy shop because of what she called the company's new predatory AI practices. The Halifax-based artist known as The Calendork announced it has removed all artwork from its Etsy shop while remaining open, citing the new insane AI policies. Matsuba, who worked in animation for seven years before losing her job, said AI was one of the major factors in that loss, and she fears shop owners are being forced to choose between earning holiday income and staying on the platform under terms that allow their content to be used for AI training.

Etsy's head of customer operations, James Ossman, said in a statement that respecting its sellers' work is central to the way Etsy runs its business. He said sellers' creative work belongs to them, and that Etsy does not use that work to train AI models designed to copy their original work or replace their creativity. Ossman said the company plans to continue discussing the policy change with sellers to clarify what it means and its intent in the terms, and he also said the company should have done more to communicate the changes coming with the updated policies. Matsuba said those discussions will not change her decision to stop selling her products on the platform, because her business is completely AI free and she does not want to participate in developing AI further.

The backlash comes as KPMG reported in 2025 that 88 per cent of tech executives surveyed believe tech companies that embrace AI will develop a competitive edge over those who do not. The same report showed that 68 per cent of respondents expect a moderate to very high return on investment related to AI investments of 10 per cent or more. Etsy has faced criticism on other fronts as well, including its ban on the sale of fur, which the CBC reported may affect Indigenous artisans most. The company says it will keep talking with sellers about the terms, while sellers like Matsuba have already decided to leave before the Dec. 16 date arrives.

stories.Headline: Diamond Restaurant bars AI-generated band flyers to prioritize human artists
stories.Summary:
Diamond Restaurant in Plaza Midwood is refusing to accept AI-generated flyers from bands performing at the venue, saying human creativity should come first. The Charlotte restaurant announced the policy, and the announcement quickly took off online, shared hundreds of times. Employee Ryan Armstrong said everybody came to the conclusion that they wanted to support local artists. He said most of these communities do not want the data centers and the great proliferation of construction using our resources. The policy starts on Sunday, November 22.

The venue's policy applies to bands promoting shows at the restaurant. Owners say they are not telling people what to think about AI, but they want to use their platform to support local artists, musicians and designers who create the work themselves. Armstrong said they thought real artists should be prioritized over this particular function of AI. Charlotte leaders continue a moratorium on new data center development through next October, giving the city more time to study their impact on neighborhoods, natural resources and infrastructure.

Armstrong, who is part of a band named Sand Dollar Starship, said as an artist himself he understands that new tools develop all the time. He said that in the case of AI, we are seeing the development of it abuse artists and intellectual property of many different contributors. Charlotte City Council member Dimple Ajmera said during the October meeting that in the next 11 months, we will have an opportunity to put guardrails in place. She said those guardrails would protect our residents, our neighborhoods and our water and the electricity grid.

The announcement was shared hundreds of times online after the restaurant took its stand. The policy affects bands promoting shows at the restaurant, along with the local artists, musicians and designers the owners say they want to support. Charlotte leaders are studying the impact of data centers on neighborhoods, natural resources and infrastructure during the moratorium. The restaurant's owners say their biggest concern is the effect AI is having on work created by real artists. The policy applies to bands promoting shows at the restaurant starting Sunday, November 22.

The articles say communities across the country are wrestling with the rise of AI. They say Charlotte leaders continue a moratorium on new data center development through next October. They say the moratorium gives the city more time to study the impact of data centers on neighborhoods, natural resources and infrastructure. Ajmera's October meeting remarks came during that moratorium. The articles give no further background on the restaurant or the bands.

The policy starts on Sunday, November 22, and applies to bands promoting shows at the restaurant. The articles do not say how the restaurant will enforce the policy or what happens to bands that submit AI-generated flyers. They do not say how long the policy will last. They do not say whether other Charlotte venues will follow. The articles leave open what the city will do when the moratorium ends next October.

stories.Headline: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang warns superintelligence may be near and urges safety work
stories.Summary:
Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang warned on November 23, 2026, that the world may already be entering the era of superintelligence. He issued the warning in a lengthy post shared on the social media platform X, formerly known as Twitter. Wang said next year could prove critical in determining whether increasingly powerful AI systems benefit humanity or lead to outcomes difficult for humans to control. He pointed to the reported proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems, as a milestone. He described the achievement as an intellectual accomplishment unlike anything humanity has seen before.

Wang said the development marks a turning point similar to December 2024, when models began acing the American Invitational Mathematics Examination with o3. He said the hardest AIME problems are much harder in terms of sheer intellectual difficulty than problems advanced engineers and business people solve day to day. He said the remaining gaps for models to greatly surpass humanity in every field are no longer intelligence, but domain-specific know-how, plumbing and experimentation. He said AI will likely become the greatest contributor of progress across nearly every field, vastly outperforming the best humans. He said models will be smart enough to automate all AI research and improve themselves in a clearly superhuman way.

Wang said it is hard to imagine humanity keeping control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement. He said it is equally hard to imagine humanity maintaining control with superintelligence 1,000 times smarter and more capable than humans in every field. He said the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, so the urgent work is safety, alignment and security. He criticized what he called lazy thinking in the AI industry, the idea that superintelligence is inevitable and the only problem is how to do it safely. He said society should not be okay with a handover of society to AI and should build technology where all humans have greater agency and empowerment.

Wang said he grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico, and that many physicists would agree the discovery of the atomic bomb is a homework problem compared to the Riemann Hypothesis. He said the Riemann Hypothesis may be the most intellectually demanding problem humanity has ever devised, which some of the most brilliant humans over the past 150 years have dedicated their lives to. He said his professors at MIT would have said the hardest intellectual problems in nearly every major field are easier than the Riemann Hypothesis, albeit with other challenges such as experimentation, data and feedback loops. He said the progress across other domains over the past two years has been immense, with coding nearly solved, extremely powerful cyber capabilities and strong agentic capabilities. He said the implications are enormous and nearly every field could be accelerated at a pace beyond what humans can understand or monitor.

Wang said he has spent much of his life in math and science. He said the math community has not fully digested the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. He said the models have become general-purpose useful aides. He said the hardest AIME problems are an extracurricular activity for teenagers. He said he strongly believes a positive future is possible but likely involves the whole industry taking meaningfully different actions from the default path.

Wang said humanity must remain actively involved in shaping its future rather than enabling society to be handed over to machines. He said the industry must depart from the default path. The article does not say when or how the Riemann Hypothesis was reportedly proved. The article does not say what actions Wang proposes beyond safety, alignment and security. The article does not say whether Meta or other companies have responded to his post. The article does not say what Wang expects to happen next beyond his call for a different path.

stories.Headline: RingCentral CFO says AI products drive growth as paid AI ARR doubles
stories.Summary:
RingCentral Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Agarwal spoke at an RBC conference, and MarketBeat reported the remarks on Saturday, November 21, 2026, describing a strategy centered on an AI customer engagement platform. He said the platform handles communications between people and increasingly between people and AI. He said the company expects AI to address routine inquiries and automate workflows, with humans stepping in when more judgment or expertise is required. He said the core business is durable and that RingCentral goes into the base to address new sales with more AI products. The conference interviewer said RingCentral AI annual recurring revenue represented about 15% of total ARR and had doubled year over year.

The measure covers customers using at least one paid AI-native product, and Agarwal said it helps the company track paid AI adoption within its customer base. RingCentral's AIR product has more than 22,000 customers, while ACE has nearly 7,000, Agarwal said. The interviewer said the Customer Engagement Bundle had 14,000 paying customers, up 50% sequentially. Agarwal said RingCentral's overall gross margin is 80%, with AI product gross margins close to that level. He identified approximately 40 billion voice minutes flowing through the platform annually as a competitive asset.

Agarwal said RingCentral is spending more than $250 million on AI investments and manages AI costs through model orchestration, inference efficiency and infrastructure efficiency. He said the company uses multiple frontier models and routes work to lower-cost models, and could evaluate open-source models over time for additional cost efficiencies. He said RingCentral sells through direct representatives, in-product discovery, a network of 16,000 partners and global service carriers. He corrected the interviewer's suggestion that about half of AI ARR comes through the partner channel, saying RingCentral had not disclosed that mix. He said an expanded partnership with NiCE gives RingCentral greater access to enterprise customers as NiCE resells its RingEX product.

Agarwal described RingCentral's enterprise business as close to $1 billion, with a generally stable demand environment, win rates and retention. He said the company continues to face comparisons with COVID-era contracts that have undergone seat and pricing rationalization and expects to move past those comparisons into the first half of next year. He declined to provide guidance for next year. He said AI products are growing from a smaller base and could contribute more to overall growth as their share of the business increases. Based on its latest guidance, he said the company expects margin expansion of about 200 basis points this year.

Agarwal said stock-based compensation is declining by about 200 basis points, supported by discipline in new share grants and the fading impact of older grants. He said RingCentral has previously stated a longer-term goal of bringing stock-based compensation to 3% to 4%. Asked about potential AI-related pressure on customer seat counts, he said RingCentral is not seeing much seat rationalization among small businesses, though it sees some at the high end of the enterprise market following headcount actions. He said selling additional products to existing customers can help offset that pressure. He said AIR, which addresses missed calls, has initially found traction with small businesses but is also being sold to larger customers.

Agarwal said AIR Pro is designed for more complex workflows, using voice AI to understand intent and take actions before handing interactions to a human when needed. He said CEB targets businesses whose employees communicate with customers but do not have a dedicated contact center, and that once customers adopt it they can also buy AIR to address missed calls and add conversational intelligence. He cited a national fitness operator that used ACE to identify the reasons customers were calling before buying AIR to automate recurring inquiries. He said Destination Pet, an existing RingCentral customer, similarly used ACE to identify call drivers and then bought AIR Pro. He said customers can use NiCE's CXone for more complex deployments or RingCentral's RingCX for simpler contact center needs.

stories.Headline: Microsoft introduces RDMA over USB4 to link Windows 11 PCs for distributed AI model runs
stories.Summary:
Microsoft revealed a new technology called RDMA over USB4 for Windows on November 22, 2026, to simplify running local AI models across multiple machines. This feature, which is currently in developer preview, allows several Windows 11 computers to link together for low-latency distributed large language model runs. By using this method, machines can move data across local memory without passing through the standard networking stack. This approach removes the need for specialized Ethernet or InfiniBand network adapters that are not typically found in standard PCs.

The system requires each connected computer to have USB4, Thunderbolt 4, or Thunderbolt 5 ports equal to the total number of machines minus one. Users must use USB4 cables for each pair of devices and ensure their applications support the Windows NetworkDirect API. To enable the feature, users must turn on Windows test signing, which requires disabling Secure Boot. Early measurements between two PCs showed that the technology cut round-trip latency for small messages to about 28 to 50 microseconds, which is roughly four times lower than Ethernet over the same link. The system scales at 40 Gbps and 80 Gbps, with the latter providing twice the bandwidth.

Microsoft stated on its blog that this technology is designed to make it easier to combine computers for AI tasks. The company noted that the developer preview currently lacks an auto-retry function for failed connections, meaning the application must handle those errors. In a test using three mini PCs with AMD Ryzen AI Max processors and 128 GB of unified memory, Microsoft ran the Qwen3-235B-A22B model across 40 Gbps ports. This specific setup achieved 18.5 tokens per second with 4-bit quantization.

The company intends to release a Windows Insider Build of this technology in the near future. While daisy-chaining USB4 cables is possible, Microsoft warned that doing so reduces overall performance. AMD reported its own results for decoding and prompt processing, claiming 21.98 tokens per second and 117.98 tokens per second respectively on its own setup. This development aims to provide an affordable way for users to expand their hardware capabilities by linking smaller PCs.

stories.Headline: One engineer runs an AI podcast network producing over 300 sports shows daily for about 5 cents
stories.Summary:
Beatline Sports, an AI-generated podcast network, launched in August and began flooding the market with daily episodes covering dozens of professional and college teams, but the shows drew little attention until their heavy use of keywords gave them traction on Apple and Spotify's search functions in November 2026, according to a Boston.com column by Chad Finn. The podcasts are hosted by AI voices trained on basic facts about a given team, and the network's graphics look suspiciously like those of the Locked On Podcast Network. A New York-based engineer named Ibnul Jaif Farabi claimed on X.com that Beatline Sports is his creation, writing that one person is producing more than 300 sports podcasts daily using custom models and agents running on CPU only. Finn listened to part of a Friday Patriots episode hosted by voices called Monica and Frank, and he wrote that the product is so lousy that even intentional promotion would not help it. The network's output requires no human hosts, as the episodes are described as an AI reading of a script of keywords about a real team rather than an actual conversation.

Farabi wrote that the whole operation costs him about 5 cents daily, a figure Finn responded to by suggesting Farabi is getting robbed. Finn noted that on a phony Jets podcast, edge rusher Will McDonald IV was referred to as Will McDonald Four, and he said he hoped for something similarly unintentionally funny on the Patriots episode but found no such luck. In the snippet Finn quoted, Monica said the offense was completely suffocated against Detroit and asked whether the team is competitive or just surviving on momentum and hope, while Frank said he felt cautious after a 35-10 loss to the Lions and that without Drake Maye at full health the ceiling is lower than most people will want to admit. Farabi is the person responsible for the network, and in his X.com post he told doubters to question their profession and said the choice is to compete or perish. Finn wrote that the podcasts entirely miss why people enjoy podcasts in the first place, which he described as hearing a conversation with knowledgeable and often humorous people listeners enjoy spending time with.

He added that Monica and Frank will never make listeners wish they were part of the conversation because it is not a conversation at all. Finn wrote that he worries about what happens when AI-generated content starts to look decent and people can no longer tell what is authentic, though he said these Beatline pods are fortunately not that. In separate media news, a Deadline report cited in the column said ESPN and ESPN2 dropped from 61 million pay-TV subscribers in 2025 to 54 million this year, down from a peak of more than 100 million fifteen years ago. Finn attributed the decline mostly to pay-TV subscriber losses across the board rather than to programming decisions. He also answered a reader question about Boston sports radio shows discussing the Celtics, ranking WEEI's Jones and Keefe and The Sports Hub's Zolak and Bertrand as the top two midday shows and Felger and Mazz at the bottom.

stories.Headline: Nvidia adds Isaac OS and Agile ONE SN humanoid to its robotics platform
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced at GTC Berlin a major expansion of its Isaac robotics development platform, adding new simulation frameworks, AI training tools, datasets and a reference humanoid robot intended to speed up work on general-purpose robotic systems. The centerpiece is Agile ONE SN, a humanoid research platform built by Agile Robots that incorporates Nvidia's Isaac GR00T foundation model and its Jetson Thor computing system. The robot stands 1.4 meters tall, weighs 40 kilograms and has 31 degrees of freedom, according to the announcement. Each of its two five-finger hands provides 20 degrees of freedom, tactile sensing and force control for dexterous manipulation. Agile ONE SN is designed for robotics researchers and developers and is scheduled to become available in early 2027.

Nvidia also introduced Isaac OS, an open-source runtime framework meant to connect robot sensors, AI models, control systems and hardware, and said Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available with tools for training robot behaviors through reinforcement learning and physics simulation. The additional resources include the SimReady Central Library, which holds more than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, and the Human 1M Dataset, which provides human activity recordings and 3D hand-tracking information for robot training. Nvidia is releasing reference workflows that combine Isaac GR00T, Cosmos world models and reinforcement learning to support synthetic data generation and robotic manipulation. The company describes Isaac as a full-stack open robotics platform giving developers models, data, simulation tools and computing systems.

Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia, said general-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed and that the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching. He said the company is giving developers the tools to bring physical AI to the world's largest industries. Zhaopeng Chen, founder and CEO of Agile Robots, said the breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale, describing one adaptable machine that learns many skills and works across environments built for people. The announcements reflect growing industry interest in combining foundation models, simulation and physical robot hardware to improve the reliability and adaptability of autonomous systems.

Several European robotics manufacturers are incorporating Nvidia technologies into their development platforms, according to the announcement. ABB Robotics is integrating Omniverse libraries with RobotStudio HyperReality to support virtual commissioning, while Kuka is using Omniverse through its Visual Components FactoryLens software. Sereact is using Isaac GR00T and Cosmos Transfer to develop its Cortex robotic manipulation platform, and Neura Robotics is applying Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to train its Neuron AI foundation model. In mobile robotics, Toyota Material Handling Europe and SoftServe report that simulation-based development can reduce commissioning time by up to 50 percent, and other companies including Schaeffler, Flexion, Franka Robotics and Universal Robots are contributing to or using the ecosystem.

Articles.Title: Nvidia expands Isaac robotics platform with new humanoid and AI development tools

stories.Headline: Dario Amodei suggests immersive video games in a private Slack chat to ease AI job losses
stories.Summary:
The Wall Street Journal published a profile of siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei around November 22, 2026. This report claims that Dario Amodei once suggested using immersive video games to reduce political strife. He allegedly made this suggestion to address joblessness caused by artificial intelligence during his time at OpenAI. The report indicates that this specific remark was made within a private Slack chat.

The reported suggestion involves using immersive video games to help people who lose their jobs because of AI. This remark occurred while Dario Amodei worked at OpenAI before he co-founded Anthropic with Daniela Amodei in 2021. NewsBytes reports that this idea was not an official plan for the company. The original Wall Street Journal article is currently behind a paywall.

The Wall Street Journal is responsible for the report, which was relayed by Techmeme and NewsBytes. NewsBytes stated that the video game idea was not an official plan. No direct response from Dario Amodei or Anthropic was found in the reviewed coverage. The exact phrase used in the Slack chat remains unknown to the public.

Critics on X voiced fears that this suggests a permanent underclass kept busy with games. People who fear AI-driven job losses are affected by the implications of this reported remark. Some defenders claim the Journal pulled a brainstorm out of context. Others argue that people need income and meaning rather than distraction.

Dario Amodei has previously warned that AI could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. In May 2025, Axios reported his warning that unemployment could reach 10 to 20 percent. He has publicly called for policy responses to a large labor shock. These public warnings contrast with the reported private chat about coping ideas.

The public is waiting for the full text of the Journal article and a formal response. It remains open whether the remark was a serious argument or a thought experiment. The date of the Slack message and the other participants are not known. Future updates may come from Anthropic newsrooms or Amodei's own channels.

stories.Headline: Luca Guadagnino says Altman has guns as Artificial opens Christmas Day
stories.Summary:
Neon is releasing Luca Guadagnino's film Artificial, about OpenAI co-founders Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever and Elon Musk, on Christmas Day, 2026. The film premiered at the New York Film Festival and the BFI London Film Fest before its theatrical release. Deadline published its Crew Call podcast interview with Guadagnino on November 21, 2026. The film stars Andrew Garfield as Sam Altman, Monica Barbaro as Mira Murati and Yura Borisov as Ilya Sutskever. Artificial currently holds a 95% fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

The film opens limited on Christmas Day, a date Deadline calls perfect for a sophisticated adult skewing awards contender. Amazon MGM Studios originally backed the movie but exited out of fear of OpenAI, because Amazon has a $50 billion investment in the Altman non-profit. CAA screened the project for Neon, which Guadagnino says was first and front and center in its passion to take over. The Simon Rich script was shot outside Altman's house in San Francisco. Dario Amodei's Anthropic went public earlier this week creating a $1.18 trillion company, with shares falling from a $111 day-of-market price to $88.91 EOD Friday.

Altman told the Vanity Fair podcast he "did not" coerce Amazon to drop Artificial, adding "I don't know anyone else who did" and "I didn't speak to Jeff Bezos." Altman said he felt like he was in a weird glitch or a simulation when he saw Garfield dressed exactly like him with the same backpack, and emphasized that Garfield "did walk like me." Altman said of the trailer, "I don't think they're going for accuracy," and called the bunker loaded with guns "an example of an inaccuracy," saying "There's no bunker with firearms on the wall." Altman admitted "I have a survivalist mindset" but said "I don't have a setup that is depicted in that trailer."

Guadagnino told Deadline, "I have validated the validating information that has been vetted: He does have guns." Guadagnino said "We were very careful that everything that was in the movie had to be approved legally," and that "the truth in this case is more extraordinary than any fiction." On Amazon exiting, Guadagnino said "I was cool because I like disruptions, very much," and called the decision to let the movie find another home "truly honorable." Guadagnino said of speculation that no studio wanted the movie, "I like to think that there was the need (by the media) to fill blank pages with nothing."

On AI as a doomsday threat, Guadagnino told Deadline, "I don't have trust and I don't have faith in humans." Guadagnino's suspicions stem from growing up during the Cold War, and he remembers "very well in 1985 when Chernobyl happened." Deadline contrasts Artificial with Sony's recent theatrical release The Social Reckoning, which it says arguably didn't resonate with the current tech era. Deadline notes the film arrives as people fear the technology will end us, whether in regards to existence or financial livelihoods.

Deadline says there has been zero ill will from Altman or OpenAI about the film, unlike the Facebook camp when The Social Network was released in 2010. Deadline cites concerns about AI including a Chatbot being at the center of 16-year old Adam Raine's suicide, and AI trespassing and impostering another company's security space. The Crew Call episode also covers why Andrew Garfield was right to play Altman and Altman's sincerity about creating guardrails for the technology. More to follow.

stories.Headline: CrowdStrike discusses acquiring Zscaler to expand AI-powered cybersecurity defenses
stories.Summary:
CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. is in talks to acquire Zscaler Inc. according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, November 21, 2026. This potential combination would be one of the largest deals in the cybersecurity industry. The two companies are discussing a deal that could come together soon. This move follows a wave of multibillion-dollar takeovers in the security market. These companies are racing to expand defenses against sophisticated attacks powered by artificial intelligence.

The deal involves Austin, Texas-based CrowdStrike and Santa Clara, California-based Zscaler in the 244 billion dollar security market. Zscaler had a market value of 32 billion dollars at the end of regular trading Friday. CrowdStrike has a market capitalization of around 235 billion dollars. Zscaler reached record revenue of 3.35 billion dollars in fiscal 2026 but has not turned an annual profit since 2018. Zscaler serves 11,000 customers in over 185 countries, including more than half of the Fortune 500.

People familiar with the matter said deliberations are ongoing and a transaction is not certain. These sources asked not to be identified because the information is confidential. Representatives for CrowdStrike and Zscaler did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The report caused Zscaler shares to rise about 16 percent after the close of trading. The deal would allow CrowdStrike to monitor threats across more parts of a company's technology infrastructure.

Cloudflare co-founder Matthew Prince said in June that AI agent traffic surpassed human internet traffic for the first time. Businesses are grappling with risks from AI-enabled attacks, benefiting providers like Palo Alto Networks Inc. and Cloudflare Inc. Zscaler's cloud-based products replace traditional VPNs from companies like Citrix and Ivanti Inc. that suspected Chinese hackers have targeted. The "SaaSpocalypse" fear suggests AI tools could allow competitors to recreate software services more cheaply. This threatens the business models of established providers.

CrowdStrike's Falcon product had a botched software update in 2024 that triggered a global IT meltdown. Alphabet Inc. bought Wiz for 32 billion dollars last year, and ServiceNow Inc. bought Armis for 7.75 billion dollars in December. Palo Alto Networks took over CyberArk for 25 billion dollars in February and bought Applied Compute for 4.5 billion dollars this month. Recent US outages affected Microsoft Corp., JPMorgan Chase & Co., United Airlines, and the National Security Agency. Gartner Inc. projects global information security spending will grow nearly 12 percent this year.

The companies will determine if these ongoing deliberations result in a final transaction. A combination would give CrowdStrike a broader role in defending corporate networks and applications. The deal would accelerate a shift toward fewer companies protecting more of the world's computers. The articles do not state when a final decision will be reached. They also do not provide a specific purchase price for the potential acquisition.

stories.Headline: Apple adds non-AI features to iOS 27 including better AutoMix and Find My redesign
stories.Summary:
Apple released iOS 27 in September 2026, and while the new Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features drew most of the attention, the update also brought a long list of non-AI changes that 9to5Mac editor Chance Miller highlighted in a piece published on November 21, 2026. In the Music app, Apple updated AutoMix with new transitions that Miller described as noticeably better and more immersive than the version that launched in iOS 26. The Photos app now offers full-resolution sharing in iCloud Shared Albums, and it also lets users save a specific video frame as a photo without taking a manual screenshot. The Clock app gained an independent alarm volume option found in Settings under Sounds & Haptics, so alarms and timers no longer have to match the ringtone volume.

The Home Screen adds an all-new extra-large widget size, including full-screen widgets for apps like Music, Photos, Weather and Calendar, and users can now swipe away the Now Playing widget from the Lock Screen. On the Lock Screen, the clock can be moved to the top widget row so it no longer covers the wallpaper. The Apple Pay checkout flow was significantly overhauled to make switching between payment cards easier, and landscape support arrived in more apps, including Music, Reminders and Weather. The Find My app has a new design with more flexible sharing options that show more specific location information without tapping on a specific person, and a built-in paste shortcut now appears above the keyboard in the next text field after something is copied. CarPlay also gained an audio scrubber for skipping to different parts of a song or podcast on the car's display.

Miller, the editor-in-chief of 9to5Mac who also hosts the site's Daily and Happy Hour podcasts, wrote that he had come to really enjoy these features and called the landscape support great as someone who keeps his iPhone docked at his desk all day. He said he was a big fan of the initial AutoMix in iOS 26 and finds the new transitions better, and he singled out the Find My redesign for showing more specific location information without extra taps. He closed by asking readers to share their own favorite non-AI features in the comments. The article does not say what happens next beyond that invitation.

stories.Headline: Benton Harbor approves City Detect AI system to scan for code violations
stories.Summary:
Benton Harbor City Commissioners approved a contract at their regular meeting this past week that will allow the city to use a more automated method of detecting code violations citywide, according to News/Talk/Sports 94.9 WSJM. The service, called City Detect, is offered to municipalities and uses vehicle-mounted cameras and artificial intelligence to spot things like building violations and illegal dumping. The department of public safety says the camera would be mounted on a city code compliance truck to conduct inspections. Commissioners amended the resolution approving the contract by adding a requirement that the Public Safety Committee receive regular reports on the program's results, and it was then approved five to three with Mayor Marcus Muhammad not present.

The contract will cost $55,000 per year and will be paid with Community Development Block Grant funds, and commissioners will be asked to renew it yearly. Public Safety told commissioners that City Detect conducted a demonstration for the inspection department, scanning 896 parcels in just a half hour and identifying issues like tall grass, sidewalk problems, boarded up windows, and trash. City Manager Alex Little said the city is not in a position to hire enough people to handle all these inspections, but technology like City Detect can help. Commissioner Sharon Henderson said the city's inspection department will only use City Detect as a first step when issuing potential citations, and that staff get a photograph and review the information rather than writing a ticket immediately.

Commissioner Juanita Henry took issue with the program, saying residents should not be burdened with surprise tickets and little human oversight, and she said she knows AI can do a lot of things but does not think this will work out well for residents because there is no human in it. Henderson said inspectors are still looking at what has been sent to them to make sure, and are not just giving people a ticket based on the system. Henry also said it is all about policy. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the yearly renewal request and the regular reports to the Public Safety Committee.

Retail investors began watching GlobalWafers after panic selling hit Nvidia and other AI leaders on November 21, 2026. This market shift followed the exit of Jensen Huang, which turned previous excitement into doubt for many investors. The company provides silicon wafers to chip manufacturers and offers upstream exposure to data center and AI demand. GlobalWafers operates across the Americas, Europe, Northeast Asia, and other Asian regions to serve its global customers. It currently holds a market capitalization of NT$233.2 billion according to the provided financial data.

It is currently moving its global capacity buildout from construction into qualification and ramp at new 12 inch fabs. These new facilities are located in Texas, Italy, and Japan to expand the company's overall production capabilities. Phase 1 tool installation is nearly complete in Texas, while the Italy line has achieved automotive grade certification. The facility in Utsunomiya, Japan, has already turned profitable and is currently operating with high utilization.

Analysts from Simply Wall St are responsible for the narrative regarding the company's global expansion and earnings potential. They stated that the company is transitioning its capacity buildout into the qualification and ramp phase for new fabs. These analysts link the company's cost base and earnings potential to its strategic expansion in three different countries. They believe the current progress in Texas, Italy, and Japan supports the company's growth in the semiconductor market. The report suggests that these developments are core threads linking the company's global capacity and future success.

The report notes that retail investors are watching the stock as a potential opportunity after recent market pullbacks. These investors are affected by the broader volatility in AI chip stocks following the leadership change at Nvidia. The analysis suggests that solid businesses can move from being crowded to ignored when market expectations reset. Some investors may see the current weakness as a signal of mispricing rather than permanent damage to the business. The text indicates that these investors are seeking established leaders in the AI and semiconductor sectors.

GlobalWafers is described as a large and profitable wafer producer tied into broader semiconductor spending and AI demand. The company's business model relies on supplying the essential silicon wafers needed by chip manufacturers worldwide. It has diversified its sales across multiple continents to mitigate risks and capture various regional market opportunities. The company's current financial standing includes significant revenue from its primary semiconductor business group. This background positions the firm as a key upstream player in the global AI hardware supply chain.

The company will continue the ramp of its new 12 inch fabs in Texas, Italy, and Japan. Future success depends on how quickly these new lines fill and the pricing the company can achieve. The articles leave open whether unseen pressures will change the speed of utilization for these new facilities. It remains unclear how the wafer mix and subsidies will reshape the company's long term financial story. Investors must wait to see if the current ramp speed leads to lasting profitability and margin growth.

stories.Headline: Writer disables all Galaxy AI features for a week and misses only two
stories.Summary:
Shimul Sood, a writer for MakeUseOf, published an article on November 21, 2026, describing a week-long experiment in which she turned off every Galaxy AI feature on her Samsung phone running One UI 9. She undertook the test after hearing chatter that Samsung might someday put some Galaxy AI features behind a paywall, although Samsung has not officially confirmed anything of that kind. She said she had been using a Samsung phone for months and could not immediately say which AI features she would be willing to pay for. Rather than guessing which features she could live without, she disabled all of them and went about her usual routine for an entire week. By the end, she found she wanted to turn only two features back on, and she said neither had anything to do with One UI 9 itself.

The two features she missed were Circle to Search, which she noted is technically a Google feature also available on Samsung phones rather than something Samsung built for Galaxy AI, and Object Eraser, an existing Galaxy AI tool in Samsung's Gallery app. She said Circle to Search proved useful on Pinterest, where she looks for home decor and interior design inspiration, because images often carry no product link and the feature let her circle a lamp or coffee table and find the item or similar alternatives. She said several of her furniture purchases began with a random picture she found on Pinterest, and that going back to manual searching felt unnecessarily tedious. Object Eraser, she wrote, let her remove unwanted elements from photos in the Gallery app instead of discarding a picture or using a third-party editing app, and while results were not always perfect with complicated backgrounds, it handled her usual fixes convincingly. Sood stressed that the experiment was not a criticism of One UI 9 or of how Samsung has implemented AI across its smartphones, but rather a reflection of how she personally uses her phone.

She wrote that she enjoys trying new AI features when they arrive, but very few become part of her routine, and she would rather have a handful of well-thought-out features than a whole suite of tools she tries once and forgets. She also said that what she missed during the week was not necessarily the AI itself but the convenience she had grown accustomed to. Once the week ended, she was in no rush to turn everything back on, and her device felt just as capable without most of its AI features. She concluded that if Samsung ever decides to charge for Galaxy AI, she at least knows where she stands, and that it would take a lot more than a growing list of AI features to convince her to open her wallet. The article does not say that Samsung has announced any pricing, timeline or other change to Galaxy AI, and it gives no further details on what happens next beyond her own intention to keep most features off.

stories.Headline: Taiwan restricts short selling to stabilize its semiconductor market after AI losses
stories.Summary:
Taiwan tightened short-selling rules on November 21, 2026, to address losses in its semiconductor-heavy market. The Financial Supervisory Commission announced these restrictions, which take effect this coming Monday. These measures follow a sharp sell-off linked to concerns about the global AI outlook. The market experienced a five-session decline of 17.5 percent for technology shares. The Taiex fell 6.23 percent on Friday to its lowest close in nearly seven months.

The new rules require short sellers to provide collateral of 150 percent, up from 130 percent. Restrictions now cover any stock that fell in the previous session, removing a 3.5 percent threshold. The FSC suspended new put warrant applications for the Taipei Exchange and the Taiwan Stock Exchange. Premier Cho Jung-tai met with agency heads on Saturday to devise these stabilization measures. Certain hedging trades by futures companies and securities firms remain exempt from these new limits.

The Financial Supervisory Commission stated its goal is market stability and orderly trading. It did not identify any particular company for intervention during this process. The regulator called on lenders to stop lending shares or recall existing loans early. It also asked lenders to avoid renewing loans at maturity, though these were not mandatory bans. The commission continues to encourage listed companies to purchase their own shares.

The Taiex closed at 36,033.29 on Friday, marking a 2,393.60-point drop. This decline was the third-largest single-session point loss in the history of the index. From its October 6 intraday record to Friday's low, the index lost 28.48 percent. Investors betting against stocks are the primary group affected by the higher collateral requirements. The Central News Agency linked the market retreat to the global AI industry outlook.

The National Financial Stabilization Fund, worth NT$500 billion, was authorized to intervene on November 6. The regulator had progressively introduced short-selling curbs since that date to support the market. A previous restriction on Thursday applied only to stocks falling at least 3.5 percent. This latest move is the first blanket restriction of its kind since 2015. These actions are part of a broader effort to stabilize the local financial environment.

The Financial Supervisory Commission will continue monitoring local conditions and global financial markets. It intends to adjust its stabilization measures accordingly based on these ongoing observations. The articles do not state when the current short-selling restrictions will be lifted. It remains open whether the regulator will implement more mandatory bans on securities lending. The long-term impact of the AI outlook on the Taiex is not determined.

Articles.Title: Taiwan tightens short-selling rules after AI-linked stock-market losses

stories.Headline: Taiwan regulators limit short selling to stabilize chip-heavy markets
stories.Summary:
Taiwanese financial regulators took drastic emergency steps on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to stabilize their chip-heavy markets. These actions followed an intense sell-off in artificial intelligence and technology stocks that rattled global investors. The main trading index in Taiwan, which relies heavily on semiconductor stocks, dropped 17.5 percent over five trading days. This local crash occurred as the Dow and S&P 500 entered correction territory by falling 10 percent.

The Financial Supervisory Commission of Taiwan announced that it would limit short selling starting on Monday. These new rules include a complete ban on short selling any stock below its closing price. However, the regulators stated that securities firms and futures companies may still borrow for hedging purposes. This intervention aims to stop the significant fluctuations currently impacting the Taiwan stock market. Such restrictions may force investors to sell long positions to raise necessary cash.

The Financial Supervisory Commission said these measures were a direct response to recent market volatility. Investor Michael Burry noted on X that he had previously warned about neoclouds and chip makers. He specifically mentioned companies like Nvidia, Coreweave, and Nebius while providing information for those who wanted to sell. Burry did not explicitly tell people to short the market, but he highlighted the risks. Some market professionals now believe the artificial intelligence trade has reached a turning point.

This situation mirrors a 2008 event when the United States Securities and Exchange Commission banned short selling for financial stocks. Former SEC Chairman Christopher Cox stated at that time that such measures should not be necessary in well-functioning markets. The American intervention during the housing market collapse largely failed to stop the decline of those stocks. Current headwinds are now reshaping the outlook for the global technology sector. Investors remain cautious as the AI bubble potentially deflates across multiple international exchanges.

stories.Headline: Baltimore Sun replaces dismissed cartoonist with AI images on opinion pages
stories.Summary:
The Baltimore Sun began publishing AI-generated illustrations on its opinion pages after dismissing its longtime cartoonist, Kevin “KAL” Kallaugher, a two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist, according to Tomorrow’s Publisher. The paper first ran syndicated cartoons and then introduced the generated images, one of which carried a caption saying it had been made using AI tools by the newspaper’s editorial staff. The Association of American Editorial Cartoonists condemned the decision in an open letter, arguing that replacing a human cartoonist with generated imagery diminishes artists’ work and weakens journalism. Kallaugher told Baltimore Fishbowl that the repeated appearance of the images made the practice seem like an ongoing editorial policy rather than an isolated experiment, and he described it as a case of AI taking people’s jobs.

The dispute also concerns attribution, because image generators have produced cartoons carrying signatures associated with real New Yorker contributors, Nieman Journalism Lab reported, including work the cartoonists said they had neither made nor endorsed. The report cautioned that imitation of an artist’s style does not by itself establish copyright infringement, and that the legal position may depend on the circumstances, including how an image is used. A report by Cartooning for Peace recommends stronger ways to identify and trace cartoons, greater transparency about the material used to train image generators, and an explicit opt-in approach to including copyrighted work in training databases. It also calls for mechanisms to address economic or moral harm caused by unauthorised use, though these are policy proposals rather than evidence that every risk has materialised in every newsroom.

FAIR’s account describes the Sun’s images as relying on generic figures and explanatory text rather than visual wit or concise satire, and it cites AI-written or AI-assisted material across opinion writing and news production, including the Financial Times’ apology after an undisclosed AI process was used to condense a column. Columbia Journalism Review has separately documented newsroom cuts at McClatchy and journalists’ concerns about the company’s use of automation, reporting that more than 90 unionised media workers across 17 publications were laid off in September 2026, while noting that a direct link between those cuts and AI plans had not been established. Journalists told the review that AI was being used for some repackaging and content-production tasks, amid uncertainty about future policy and the effect of staff losses on coverage. The professional and policy responses call for transparency and protection for artists, and the challenge for news organisations is to show readers where automation is used without obscuring who is responsible for the work.

stories.Headline: Cipher Digital ranks sixth among most overvalued AI stocks as short interest hits 18 percent
stories.Summary:
Cipher Digital Inc., which trades on Nasdaq under the ticker CIFR, ranked sixth on a list of the ten most overvalued AI stocks according to short sellers, published by Insider Monkey and reported by Yahoo Finance on November 21, 2026. The company's shares had lost more than half of their market value during 2026, as investors grew wary of its aggressive AI data center expansion, its financing needs and its valuation. Short interest in the stock had risen to 18 percent, reflecting bets that the company may struggle to deliver the earnings and cash flow needed to justify its premium valuation. The article frames the central issue as Cipher's ability to complete its transition from Bitcoin mining to AI and high-performance computing infrastructure and to generate sustainable cash flow from that business.

The company's net debt stood at approximately $3.08 billion as of September, a significant burden for a business still scaling its HPC operations, and the article notes concerns that debt-servicing costs and future financing needs will weigh on shareholder returns. Cipher recognized its first HPC lease revenue of $5.85 million in the third quarter of 2026, after rent commenced at its Black Pearl facility, which the article says shows the transition remains relatively early. The company has secured long-term agreements carrying $9.1 billion in contracted revenue, which the article cautions should not be confused with immediate cash flow or guaranteed profits. The stock trades at approximately 18.24 times sales, a valuation the article says leaves little room for execution setbacks, and the company could also come under pressure if data center construction takes longer than expected.

The article places Cipher within a broad market sell-off driven by renewed concerns about elevated AI valuations and uncertainty over whether the huge capital committed to AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns. It reports that the rout wiped out about $3 trillion in S&P 500 market capitalization in early November, as the Nasdaq recorded its largest single-day decline in 19 months. Michael Burry raised concerns that AI infrastructure companies could be relying on increasingly complicated financing arrangements that may become unsustainable, while RSM chief economist Joe Brusuelas was wary of a wholesale bursting of the AI bubble as uncertainty surrounding Nvidia undermined confidence among lenders and investors. Barclays chief market strategist Julien Lafargue warned that the sell-off was exposing the growing cost of financing AI infrastructure, and Goldman Sachs strategists warned that the outlook for AI investment and corporate profit margins in 2028 and beyond remains highly uncertain. Anthropic's IPO raised $81 billion but failed to reverse the broader weakness in AI-related stocks, while Morgan Stanley argued the November sell-off was excessive and presented a buying opportunity.

stories.Headline: Walmart launches a $120 Sam's Club Plus and Walmart+ bundle as Sparky lifts basket sizes 40 percent
stories.Summary:
Walmart launched a combined membership for Sam's Club Plus and Walmart+ on October 20, 2026, to attract busy households. Chief executive John Furner announced the bundle as a way to create the most essential membership in the United States. The company is also utilizing Sparky, an AI shopping assistant that debuted in June 2025, to increase customer spending. This digital tool operates in French, Spanish, and English across Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The new bundle costs $120 per year, which is a significant reduction from the $400 cost for separate memberships.

Existing Walmart+ members who pay $90 can upgrade to this plan, while Sam's Club Plus members are able to link their accounts. The strategy has already brought in a couple of million new customers for Sam's Club. Third quarter results ended October 31, 2026, showing revenue of $188.8 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $0.65. John Furner stated that the company is focusing on services rather than just price to drive growth. He explained that Sparky helps families save time by providing recipes and one click ordering for ingredients.

Furner noted that the consumer remains resilient and consistent, particularly among higher income households over the last few years. He also mentioned that the company can now reach 96 percent of the U.S. population with three hour delivery. The company reported that U.S. usage of Sparky rose 129 percent year over year, with users filling baskets 40 percent larger. Walmart raised its full year adjusted earnings per share guidance to between $2.84 and $2.89. However, Sam's Club operating income fell 15.8 percent because part of the membership fees are now allocated to Walmart U.S. The upcoming holiday quarter will test if these memberships and AI tools successfully increase shopper loyalty.

stories.Headline: Unloved stocks like Campbell's and Clorox rally as the AI trade loses steam
stories.Summary:
The artificial intelligence trade is losing steam, and investors may be able to find some stock market winners by digging deep in the dustbin. The unwind of the AI trade dragged the Nasdaq Composite to a loss on the year, now off 2.7% in 2026. The past month has been especially brutal for the tech-heavy index, which has lost 14% in the period. However, several non-AI stocks that are widely disliked by analysts may offer refuge from the tech-driven sell-off. Some of these names, such as the Campbell's Company, are touting solid gains in an otherwise rocky time for the market.

Just one analyst out of 23 rates Campbell's a buy, according to FactSet, and shares are up nearly 20% in the past month. BTIG chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky said in a note to clients that nobody owns the stock and it is universally unloved, which he called a very powerful set-up. He added that with a volume pocket up towards the $30 level, the stock can see a sharp move higher. CNBC used FactSet data to screen for other unloved stocks in the S & P Composite 1500 that have outperformed the overall market over the past month. All of the picks have buy ratings from no more than 10% of the analysts who cover them.

Clorox is one of the most hated stocks on Wall Street, with the majority of analysts rating it a hold, and on average analysts see shares suffering an 11% decline over the next 12 months. Despite all of that, Clorox has jumped roughly 20% over the past month. JetBlue Airways is another unpopular stock that has rallied recently, and according to FactSet just one analyst has a buy rating on the airline. JetBlue's finances have been under pressure as it contends with higher fuel costs, but shares have risen 14% over the past month and the company has fleshed out its new corporate strategy.

Boston Beer has also seen share gains as of late, with the stock up nearly 13% over the past month. The maker of Twisted Tea lifted its full-year guidance in October, calling for adjusted earnings of $9 to $10.50 per share and topping the FactSet consensus estimate of $8.90 a share. That hasn't translated to optimism on the Street, however, since just 6.7% of analysts who cover the stock have a buy rating on it, according to FactSet. Other unpopular stocks that made the list include Lululemon and Prudential Financial.

stories.Headline: SDMC presents home physical AI concept and signs Altice Labs lab deal
stories.Summary:
SDMC took part in the Google TV Summit 2026 in Bangkok as an invited speaker for the third year in a row and presented its AI strategy for the home under the theme of building the future of home physical AI with Google. At the event the company showed an innovative product concept built on Google's ecosystem and technologies, and it worked with Amlogic to push Edge AI innovation further. Together with Altice Labs it gave a joint presentation on physical AI in the home environment with a focus on television, and the two companies signed a memorandum of understanding to set up joint innovation laboratories for home AI. The company described physical AI in the home as intelligence that senses conditions in the house, understands context and acts in the physical environment, and it treats the television and living room as the centre of the experience with a home AI agent.

SDMC presented the Cedar Display Hub, a concept prototype that combines an Android TV streaming dock with a companion second screen, and the demonstrations included AI recaps without interrupting playback, family games across screens and home camera highlights on the television. The Cedar combines Edge AI based on Gemma with cloud reasoning powered by Gemini for context-aware assistance, while the Display Hub with the A311Y3 chip uses voice and face recognition to tell family members apart. The AI NAS Frame with the S905D5 chip supports recognition, classification and search of family photos stored locally, and SDMC is taking part in the Google Cloud programme for proactive acceleration of physical AI. For operators the SDMC home AI portfolio builds on existing television and broadband services, with the AI Streaming Box bringing AI-enhanced entertainment, whole-home control and family security to the television.

The Google TV Projector extends premium viewing and the AI Fiber Gateway provides Wi-Fi 8 and XGS-PON connectivity, while AI Operation adds proactive monitoring, unified device management and closed-loop support. In the joint presentation SDMC explained how home AI agents complement personal assistants and how AI at the edge of cloud and local devices enables family experiences on two screens, and Altice Labs drew on Sophia, its upcoming MEO television assistant, to discuss the shift from responding to requests to proactive help. Under the memorandum the two companies plan a Joint Innovation Laboratory for Home AI that combines SDMC's integration capabilities with Altice Labs' operator expertise to explore family assistance, home security and whole-home control. Selected scenarios are planned for a field pilot in Portugal, with commercial validation scheduled for 2027, and the aim of the joint efforts is to make physical AI for the home useful for families and viable for operators.

stories.Headline: Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge publish an AI-aided Navier-Stokes blowup proof
stories.Summary:
NYU professor Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge published an AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup on November 21, 2026. They claim this new mathematical work closes a loophole found in a previous solution provided by OpenAI. The researchers used large language models to assist in the writing of their complex mathematical proof. This publication occurred two months after OpenAI had scooped them on the same famous mathematical problem. The proof follows a computer-assisted path once the numerical profile is established for the equations.

The proof addresses the 167-year-old problem of finite-time blow-up for the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations. It involves the unforced Navier-Stokes singularity and the unforced Euler singularity, as well as the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. The work was shared via GitHub and the NYU Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences. It utilizes a numerical profile to establish the singularity formation within the three-dimensional Euler equations. The researchers used AI to help polish the final write-up of the mathematical proof.

Tristan Buckmaster stated that the team could not risk waiting to publish after being scooped by OpenAI. He explained that the resulting Navier-Stokes write-up is unpolished because it was heavily assisted by LLMs. Buckmaster noted that the proof follows a well-trodden path once the numerical profile is in hand. Levent Alpöge is an employee at Anthropic who collaborated on this AI-aided mathematical solution. Both authors believe their work successfully addresses the loophole left by the earlier OpenAI solution.

The research is discussed by Terence Tao and mentioned in reports by Euronews and the MindStudio Blog. Some observers on Hacker News and Reddit claim that AI just solved the real Navier-Stokes problem. The work affects the broader scientific community interested in fluid dynamics and the capabilities of AI. Matt Rosoff commented on a Wall Street Journal article regarding the balance of the reporting. The proof is now available for review on GitHub and the NYU Courant website.

The articles provide background on a volatile week for AI companies and the broader stock market. Anthropic recently had the largest IPO in history, pricing shares at 83 dollars to value the firm at 1.5 trillion dollars. However, Anthropic stock closed down 8.5 percent at 88.91 dollars on its second day of trading. Nvidia shares fell 14 percent on Friday, contributing to a massive weekly wipeout for chip stocks. The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6 percent on Friday, marking its worst run in over six years.

The mathematical community will now evaluate if the proof truly closes the loophole in the OpenAI solution. The articles leave open whether this proof will be formally accepted as the final solution. Market analysts continue to monitor if the AI investment boom is slowing down or entering a correction. It remains unclear how the SEC probe into Nvidia accounting will affect future AI hardware investments. The long-term impact of AI-aided proofs on traditional mathematics is not fully detailed.

stories.Headline: Researchers find AI routers leak sensitive user data despite privacy policies
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Dragos and PrivacyAffairs discovered that AI routers leaked sensitive user data. They used canary credentials in requests to services like OpenRouter and Vercel. This testing occurred over several months leading up to November 21, 2026. The team planted two million digital tripwires to detect unauthorized access. They found that privacy was often broken and keys were stolen.

The test used Amazon Web Services access keys and functioning credentials for empty accounts. It also included SSH passwords, unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. OpenRouter warned that prompts sent to MiniMax models may have been read. This affected requests from September 23 at 15:06 to October 19 at 18:25 UTC. Data went through Novita, StreamLake, and AtlasCloud back to MiniMax in China.

Researcher HD Moore stated that the AI supply chain needs canaries to find leaks. He assembled the collection of fake credentials to test for potential leakage. OpenRouter sent emails confirming that third parties may have read specific account requests. The company noted that 579 requests to MiniMax models and ERNIE 4.5 VL were affected. These findings show that Zero Data Retention policies did not prevent the leaks.

Nate Berkopec said he is removing OpenRouter and Vercel Gateway from his stack. He believes the risk is not worth it and is moving to Baseten. Dr. Abeba Birhane said keeping secrets private in prompts is now a daunting task. Kyle DH noted that auditing the full data processor supply chain is not possible. Others warned that users should not enter any confidential information into these systems.

The researchers tested a sprawling network of AI services and LLM gateways. These gateways act as resellers of AI processing for their customers. The study revealed that these intermediaries can be a security nightmare for users. The articles describe the AI supply chain as a series of closed source processors. This structure makes it difficult to know how data is actually behaving.

The researchers will continue to monitor how these AI routers handle sensitive data. Users are now being warned to avoid using AI routers for private information. The articles do not state if OpenRouter or Vercel have fixed the leaks. It remains unclear how many other providers are compromised by similar issues. The reports leave open whether Zero Data Retention policies can ever be trusted.

stories.Headline: ElevenLabs releases ElevenAI desktop app for dictation and meeting capture
stories.Summary:
ElevenLabs has released a new desktop app called ElevenAI, which combines voice dictation and meeting capture in a single tool, according to a review published by Mint on 21 November 2026 and written by Jaspreet Bindra and Anuj Magazine. The app turns speech into text in any application where a user can type, and it records in-person or online meetings on the user's own machine without a bot joining the call. After a meeting it generates a summary, labels the speakers and drafts follow-up messages. The reviewers describe it as a way to spend less time documenting conversations and more time acting on what was agreed.

The app supports dictation in more than 90 languages, removes filler words and fixes punctuation as it converts speech to text. Users can add product and distributor names once so they are spelled correctly everywhere, and they can ask questions across past meetings, such as what was promised to a distributor on credit terms last month. Through MCP, the app connects to tools such as Claude or ChatGPT so a user can turn a week of client meetings into a one-page sales update. According to the article, audio is not stored and transcript history stays on the user's Mac.

The article names Jaspreet Bindra, co-founder and CEO of AI&Beyond, and Anuj Magazine, its co-founder, as the authors, and says the tool was excerpted from Leslie D'Monte's weekly TechTalk newsletter. The reviewers say the tools featured in the section showed clear value based on internal testing, and that their recommendations are independent and not influenced by the tool creators. They present ElevenAI as solving the problem that meeting bots can make clients wary while in-person discussions often go unrecorded. The article gives the access link as elevenlabs.io/elevenai and does not say what happens next.
