stories.Headline: Anthropic shares fall 8.5 percent as AI stocks lose $4 trillion in a week
stories.Summary:
Anthropic’s initial public offering, the biggest ever, stumbled on its second day of trading on Friday, November 20, 2026, when the company’s shares dropped as much as 15 percent to just 5 cents above the IPO price before closing down 8.5 percent at $88.91, still 7 percent above the IPO price, according to The Wall Street Journal. The slide came one day after the stock opened for trading on Thursday shortly before noon more than 30 percent above the IPO price, then lost steam through the day and closed up 17 percent. The drop shed some $109 billion from Anthropic’s market value and unfolded alongside declines in Nvidia, Meta and Oracle that sealed a $4 trillion wipeout for major AI stocks over the week. A blame game has begun among investors, who cite everything from angry fund managers shut out of the offering to poor planning by banks. The offering raised more than $100 billion in the IPO and a concurrent share sale, and more than half of the $81 billion worth of IPO shares went to investors who already held stakes in the company, including Altimeter Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures, an unusually high portion reflecting executives’ desire to reward early backers.

Some people familiar with the matter estimated that around 60 percent of firms that asked to buy shares at the IPO price, many of them hedge funds and large mutual funds, got nothing, while BlackRock received about half of the roughly $10 billion allocation it requested. Anthropic also allocated significant portions to big investment firms such as Citadel, leading some shut-out investors to speculate that the company favored large users of its Claude model. A unique provision let some current and former employees immediately sell around 300 million shares, worth around $26 billion at the IPO price, which likely added downward pressure, and another roughly 300 million shares will become available to trade on December 15. People close to Anthropic and its lead underwriters maintain the IPO is a success, emphasizing the money raised and that the stock remains above its IPO price despite one of the worst market selloffs in history. One hedge-fund manager wondered whether the bankers who decide when and at what level to open shares for trading overshot the opening price, creating downward momentum that can be hard to reverse.

From the bankers’ perspective the offering remains a success as long as shares stay above the IPO price, but should they fall below it, one stabilizing tool would be unavailable: the company announced Friday morning that the so-called green-shoe option, which lets underwriters distribute 15 percent more shares and buy them back to buoy the stock, had already been exercised. The turmoil endangers the ambitions of Anthropic’s chief rival OpenAI, which is eager to make its own public market debut next year and is in the process of another mega fundraising round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. In San Francisco, several AI employees said they largely disregarded the selloff, preoccupied instead by an Anthropic mathematician’s claim on Friday that Claude had solved a Millennium Prize Problem that has stumped humans for 167 years, which many took as a sign that AI was outpacing human intelligence. Those employees also noted that even at its lower price, many Anthropic employees’ shares are still worth millions of dollars more than they were at the start of the week.

stories.Headline: Teacher Afeeda Kallil argues institutions lack emotional infrastructure to handle AI in education
stories.Summary:
A few months before November 2026, Afeeda Kallil watched a senior teacher in a Sharjah staffroom go quiet after a 15-year-old corrected her mid-sentence using a chatbot transcript on his phone. The teacher had spent 22 years in the profession and had once commanded a room simply by entering it. Kallil, who has spent two decades in classrooms, described the moment as a small collapse of authority, dignity and belonging happening in real time. She wrote about it in The Hindu, published on November 21, 2026, arguing that public debate on AI in education is loud but narrow. Kallil said almost no language exists for what happens to people and institutions as AI enters education.

She argued that institutions are held together by shared meanings about who is permitted to know, who may speak and whose judgement is trusted. Every major technology reorganises those meanings, she wrote, and AI is doing so at unprecedented speed. She said most AI policies misread this by treating AI as a tool to deploy, when it is reshaping how students understand themselves, how teachers understand their worth and how institutions define a good outcome. Kallil is responsible for the argument, drawing on her two decades in classrooms and the Sharjah episode she witnessed. She wrote that what no institution has yet built is the emotional infrastructure to hold AI, even though AI has already entered education.

She placed the responsibility with institutions and policymakers whose AI policies, in her view, treat the technology as a simple tool. Her account is a first-person reflection rather than a report of a policy decision or an official response. The article offers context rather than a sequence of events, describing a gap between fast-moving AI adoption in schools and universities and the slower work of rebuilding trust and meaning. It gives no dates for next steps, no planned policies and no named officials beyond the author's own account. What happens next, in the article's framing, depends on whether institutions build that emotional infrastructure rather than continuing to deploy AI as a tool alone.

stories.Headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent and posts 28% revenue growth
stories.Summary:
Meta rallied 6.55% to close at $653.69, driven by strong Q2 advertising revenue and the introduction of Muse, its new consumer AI agent. TradingKey author Arslan Ali wrote the analysis, dated Sep 10, 2026. Meta opened at $653.69 with a latest completed close nearly matching the chart supplied of $653.47. The stock approached the $658.01 to $659.05 resistance level after a series of higher highs and higher lows. The rally was attributed to the introduction of Muse, Meta's AI agent that can work across email, travel, payments and other applications.

Muse is available as a free product and two service tiers at $20 and $100 per month for heavy use. Meta delayed the product from an earlier planned launch in the hopes of improving safety, and now uses isolated virtual machines combined with system monitoring for some activities. Q2 revenue was $60.80 billion, up 28% year over year, and Family daily active people rose to 3.60 billion. Ad impressions rose 14% and the average cost for each ad rose 12%. Capital expenditures were $31.08 billion in Q2 and operating cash was $31.86 billion, with free cash flow dropping to $784 million.

Management still expects to spend $130 billion to $145 billion on capital expenditures for fiscal year 2026, with total expenses expected in the range of $165 billion to $169 billion. For Q3, management still expects revenue in the range of $61 billion to $64 billion with no formal guidance for a downward adjustment. In Q2, costs and expenses increased 55% to $42.03 billion, largely attributable to legal and severance charges. Operating income fell 8% to $18.78 billion, and operating margin decreased to 31% from 43%. Reuters reported that internal testing uncovered several reliability and security issues, including cases in which the agent exposed or mishandled private information.

Australia has proposed legislation in which social networks with a significant user base must provide users the choice to control their algorithmic feeds, including a choice to view content from accounts they follow. The 1-hour structure is bullish, with higher highs and higher lows, and price trading well above the trend line at around $596.90 and the moving average. The next resistance is likely around $658.01 to $659.05, and if this level is broken price may rise to around $669.59, with $683.99 the next level after that. RSI is around 79, above the 70 overbought level and the signal line around 73. If price falls, support may be found around $638.72, and below this support price may drop to $624.31 and $605.54.

The article gives key levels: last close around $653.69, breakout resistance $658.01 to $659.05, first bullish target $669.59, second target $683.99, first support $638.72, secondary support $624.31, third support $605.54 and fourth support $596.90. The article says the stock rally is interesting for two reasons: strong fundamentals for Meta's advertising and the launch of Muse, which provides a direct consumer AI activity path. The article says this path is potentially very large, but in combination with strong advertising fundamentals, security, reliability and return on the $130 billion to $145 billion 2026 capex plan are of equal concern. The article says a sustained hourly close above $659.05 would confirm that the stock can move past the current resistance zone and justify targeting $669.59 followed by $683.99. The article says the author remains bullish as long as $638.72 holds but $659.05 in combination with RSI near 79 suggests a slight pullback.

The article says the case for the investment is shifting toward the company's ability to spend tens of billions of dollars on new AI related infrastructure to create new profitable products, with Muse the most recent example. The article says Meta positioned its AI offerings differently from other early stage AI companies because it has a large profitable advertisement platform, so AI need not become its own profitable business. The article says Meta can fund many experiments and heavy AI usage. The article says investors are very concerned that Meta's returns on its core business are diminishing, and with the large capital investments investors want to see returns on data centers, chips and AI models. The article says the margin contraction is worth noting, and that in the next earnings release strong revenue must not be the only metric of concern, with more attention to capex, free cash flow and whether margins can stabilize.

The article says a clear break above $659.05 would justify targeting $669.59 and then $683.99. The article says the success of Muse could validate Meta's move away from ad based products and services to something more AI related. The article says the adoption of Muse will prove to be a strong revenue stream from AI. The article says the trust required to use this AI is much greater than a standard chatbot, and that an AI agent the public can use to make payments or send emails becomes more useful the more autonomous it is, but the reputational cost of mistakes becomes greater and much faster. The article says the AI industry is likely to face more scrutiny, especially regarding safety and accountability, which makes Muse a major real-world consumer AI-agent test.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Civil aviation minister Rammohan Naidu urges parents and educators to revive children's reading habits
stories.Summary:
Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu on Saturday called for a renewed reading movement among children, saying books were more important than ever when technology and artificial intelligence were increasingly shaping young minds. He spoke while inaugurating the two-day Vizag Junior Literary Fest at Hawa Mahal on Beach Road in Visakhapatnam, an event The Hindu reported on November 21, 2026. He said that while technology made information readily accessible, books helped children develop creativity, curiosity and the ability to ask meaningful questions. He told the gathering that technology is answering questions, but books will help children write the right questions, and he pointed to the growing challenge of keeping children interested in reading.

He also cautioned against declining attention spans and urged parents and educators to cultivate reading habits from an early age. Mr. Naidu said children should understand the value of both books and technology, and recalling his childhood he said his home had a room full of books that was called a library, stressing the need to revive the culture of reading. Referring to the festival's theme of collaboration, he said reading exposed children to different perspectives and encouraged them to engage with ideas beyond their own, and that unlike a conversation with someone across the table, reading enabled a silent debate within one's mind. Describing the festival as an investment in the minds of the next generation, he compared it with the investment announcements made at the CII Partnership Summit in Andhra Pradesh the previous week, saying lakhs of crores of rupees in investments had been announced for Andhra Pradesh and North Andhra but the festival was much more powerful because it invested in the minds of the future.

He described the Vizag Junior Literary Fest as an important event on the national literary festival calendar and one of the major children's literary festivals in South India, and urged the young audience to return for the next edition after reading more books, telling them the festival was theirs. Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat also spoke about the impact of AI on reading habits and said literary festivals had become even more relevant in the present context. Earlier, Sonal Sarda, one of the festival's directors, urged children to ask questions and interact with authors and storytellers, while fellow directors Priya Uppalapati and Sandhya Venugopal Godey said the festival had brought together some of the finest authors and storytellers. They also highlighted sessions planned for parents, particularly those focusing on storytelling, and emphasised that a child's introduction to stories began at home.

Mime artiste Kunal Motling entertained the audience with an interactive performance at the inaugural programme, and the day's sessions concluded with a theatrical performance by Chennai-based theatre group Crea Shakthi. The concluding day's sessions will run from 10.30 a.m. till 7 p.m. on Sunday.

stories.Headline: AI cheating scandal and top scorer’s death push South Korea to question exam fairness
stories.Summary:
The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test concluded amid confusion tied to emergency disaster alert tones and the death of Lee Jin-woo, the perfect scorer on this year’s Legal Education Eligibility Test. A scandal over artificial intelligence cheating fuelled turmoil right up to CSAT day. The articles say the episode laid bare the underbelly of a “republic of exams” where grades are treated as the measure of success. They say ranking people by tests is considered the fairest approach there. The government reached for button stickers and bounty rewards as AI technology advanced by the day.

Lee, a student in the School of Dentistry at Seoul National University, gained fame in July by earning perfect scores across all sections of the LEET, in reading comprehension and logical reasoning. With the single title of the first LEET perfect scorer, he went through media interviews and YouTube appearances and became a number one best-selling author. On the 15th, along with the cheating confession by the top passer on the tax accountant exam, suspicions were raised about Lee as well. What followed, the articles say, was doxxing, complaints and the opening of an investigation. Less than five days passed before his death.

On the 19th, the day he was found dead after announcing a plan for public verification, parts of the police search were even broadcast live by some YouTubers. On the 22nd, President Lee Jae Myung emphasised a “fair world” and the “principle of fairness” and pledged strict punishment for cheating and a sweeping review of test administration. The police also announced a policy of continuing their cheating investigation even after the death of Lee, contrary to ordinary procedure. Professor Shin Jae-yong of the Department of Business Administration at Seoul National University wrote on an online community that all of this is an extremely, quintessentially Korean situation. He said the public, the publishing world, YouTubers and the media floated Lee to the very sky and are the quickest to cut ties once facts are revealed.

The civic group Transparent Bag Strap, which has criticised an academic-elitist society, said on the 18th that people should not trust the fairness of exams and should question a society that evaluates people by exams. It said what matters is not strengthening procedural fairness to line students up more precisely but posing questions to a reality in which life opportunities differ excessively according to test results. Sociologist Dr. Oh Chan-ho said the case of Lee can also seem like a sad self-portrait of Korean society that shows how important it is judged to land a big hit on a test. He said higher test scores were until now seen as proof of being smart and logical, but the AI cheating scandal has forced a fundamental question about what meaning this format of exam has. Kim Dong-chun, emeritus professor at Sungkonghoe University, said it is unreasonable to rank people strictly by scores, eliminate the majority to create losers and let winners continue to enjoy vested interests.

The articles give as background that last June, immediately after controversy erupted over fabricated Harvard credentials, Kim Min-ji, author of a book, died. They say that even if fabricating academic records and gaining private benefit by fraud rightfully deserves criticism, the repeated pattern of people embroiled in fake credentials controversies dying under excessive denunciation demands reflection. Some interpret the sweeping impact of the AI cheating issue as stemming from its shaking of the very foundations of the exam system that has long functioned in Korean society as the standard for allocating social status and resources. Anxiety is growing that the assessment regime, sustained by the proposition that exams are fairest, can waver in the face of advances in AI technology. In particular, with controversy erupting on the eve of the CSAT, voices gained force saying that fairness may be damaged.

Long advocated out of concern over potential misuse in illegal filming crimes, calls to restrict the distribution and possession of micro-cameras have gained momentum only after being linked with the fairness discourse ahead of the CSAT. More fundamentally, some argue for reexamining the test-centred evaluation system that this incident has brought to light. The articles leave open how the promised review of test administration will proceed and what the continuing police investigation will establish. They do not say what the review will change or when it will report. They do not say what the investigation will conclude about the suspicions raised on the 15th.

stories.Headline: Dario Amodei tells Jamie Dimon that Anthropic prioritizes company culture over technical talent in hiring
stories.Summary:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon to discuss his strict hiring philosophy. This conversation occurred a few days before the company launched its 1.4 trillion dollar initial public offering. Amodei explained how he prioritizes company culture over raw technical ability to keep the firm unified. He stated that this approach has been a non-negotiable rule since the company first began. The CEO still spends much of his own time focusing on talent and culture.

The company requires every candidate to go through a mandatory culture interview to protect how teams work. Amodei and six co-founders agreed on day one to prioritize these values after leaving their previous firm. Anthropic screens out jerks, spotlight-stealers, and people who have no indifference to public benefit. Dario Amodei is 43 and holds a PhD in biophysics and computational neuroscience from Princeton University. Daniela Amodei is 39 and graduated with an English degree from the University of California, Santa Cruz.

Dario Amodei told Dimon that turning down deeply talented people who do not fit the culture is disciplined. He said that sticking to these standards consistently creates a team where everyone is on the same side. Amodei noted that it is painful in the short run to pass up top technical talent. He explained that companies struggle when incredible teams work against each other instead of working together. The CEO believes that internal fighting wastes the energy of a highly skilled workforce.

The hiring process affects brilliant engineers who are rejected despite their skills because they are considered jerks. Amodei believes that people who try to steal the show do not work well with others. He argues that the company must avoid those who are not oriented toward the public benefit. Daniela Amodei stated that developing artificial intelligence with safety in mind was a central goal for founders. She told ABC News that AI could help in healthcare and with fighting various diseases.

Dario and Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic in 2021 with five other former colleagues from the rival OpenAI. Dario previously worked at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and at the Google Brain AI lab. He later served as VP of research at OpenAI and helped develop GPT-2 and GPT-3 models. Daniela worked at Stripe as a risk manager and served as VP of safety and policy. She also worked on the campaign for former Pennsylvania congressman Matt Cartwright and spent time on Capitol Hill.

Anthropic will begin publicly trading on Thursday in one of the biggest market debuts in history. Dario Amodei has clashed with the Trump administration over the use of the company's AI models. He has written essays arguing that people underestimate both the radical upside and the bad risks. The articles note that all seven co-founders are still at the company today. It remains open how the company will handle business or political pressure after its Wall Street debut.

stories.Headline: Meta has never announced or released a model named Llama 5
stories.Summary:
There is no Llama 5, and Meta has never announced or released a model by that name, according to felloai.com. Meta's last Llama release was Llama 4, on 5 April 2025. Meta's 2026 models ship under a new name, Muse, and its newest open-weight model is Muse Spark Open, released on 15 October 2026. Pages still claim Llama 5 launched in April or June, with 600 billion parameters and a multi-million-token context window. The article checks each of those claims against Meta's own pages and its Hugging Face account.

Meta's meta-llama Hugging Face account has no Llama 5, and its newest model was uploaded in April 2025. Pages claim Llama 5 shipped on 8 April, around 15 April and 17 June 2026, and one has been retracted, with none citing a Meta source. The next Meta flagship, codenamed Avocado, shipped as the closed Muse Spark on 8 April 2026. Muse Spark Open, with 816B parameters and 42B active, arrived on 15 October 2026 and runs on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios. Manifold traders give a model named Llama 5 about a 1% chance before 2027.

RAGyfied published a page on 11 April 2026 saying Llama 5 had been released three days earlier, with 600 billion parameters and a 5 million token context window. RAGyfied has since corrected it, saying the earlier version relied on an unverified secondary report and that no Meta source supports it. Tech Jacks Solutions published a brief saying Meta released Llama 5 on approximately April 15, 2026, as a 600B+ parameter open-weights model that can refine its own weights. The brief gives arXiv 2604.11002 as the technical report, but that number belongs to a physics paper on leptogenesis, and its Meta AI Blog link points to an unrelated hardware reseller's post about Claude. TokenCalculator still runs a review saying Meta released three Llama 5 models on June 17, Scout, Maverick and Behemoth, which are the Llama 4 model names.

AI Omni Feed's release watch, last updated on 7 September 2026, opens with a claim that Meta has confirmed Llama 5's training run is ahead of schedule, and it links to no Meta statement. The page also lists a 1 trillion parameter design, a 256K context window and benchmark scores, all described as internal and none published by Meta. Kol Tregaskes, who tracks AI releases on X, said in October 2025 that he did not think it was news to say Llama 5 is cancelled, that the new Meta lab were to build a new model, and that the Llama name had been stained from the Llama 4 mess. Bloomberg reported in December 2025 that Meta was shifting focus to a model codenamed Avocado, expected to launch closed so Meta could sell access directly. According to The Decoder's summary of that report, the open approach had lost support inside Meta after Llama 4's disappointing reception, and the work sat with Alexandr Wang's new Meta Superintelligence Labs.

Meta launched Muse Spark on 8 April 2026 as the first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, and The Next Web reported that it was the model known internally as Avocado. Muse Spark is closed, powers the Meta AI app and meta.ai, and Meta opened only a private API preview at launch. Meta released Muse Glimmer on 10 August 2026, a 30 billion parameter model under the Apache 2.0 license, distilled from Muse Spark and, according to Hugging Face, ideal for running locally. On the same day, CNBC reported, Mark Zuckerberg said Meta would also open the weights of Muse Spark 1.2. Meta released Muse Spark Open on 15 October 2026, three days after launching its closed flagship, Muse Wonder.

Meta's official AI account announced Muse Spark Open as the most capable US open-weight model to date, built for coding and agentic work, with 816B total and 42B active parameters, a 1M token context window, and native multimodality across text, image, video and audio. Hugging Face's launch post puts the BF16 checkpoint at about 1.5 TB, and Meta says the model was optimized for Apple's Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra chip using Apple's MLX framework. Meta's announcement says each Mac Studio lets its GPU use up to 512 GB of memory, so two machines can hold an entire model, and Engadget estimated that four Mac Studios with 256 GB each costs roughly $38,000. Mark Zuckerberg credited Apple directly on launch day, saying Muse Spark Open runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with John Ternus and Apple. Meta releases Muse Spark Open under a new Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, not under the Llama license and not under a standard open source license such as Apache 2.0, and Meta has not said which Muse Spark version the open checkpoint matches.

The table in the article shows Llama 4 Scout and Maverick released 5 April 2025 under the Llama 4 license, Llama 4 Behemoth announced but never released, Muse Spark 1.0 to 1.3 released 8 April 2026 and updated to 2 September, Muse Glimmer 30B released 10 August 2026 under Apache 2.0, Muse Wonder released 12 October 2026, and Muse Spark Open released 15 October 2026 under the Muse Model License. Meta's April 2026 launch post for Muse Spark says it reaches the same capability with over an order of magnitude less compute than the previous model, Llama 4 Maverick. The article says the cancellation claim is the only one the record supports, and even that was a reading of events rather than an announcement. The table grades the 8 April claim as retracted, the April 15 claim as false, the 17 June claim as false, the training-finish claim as unsupported, the Avocado-closed report as confirmed, and the cancellation claim as likely but never official. The article says the table shows where each Meta model family stands as of 9 November 2026.

Llama 5 has no release date, and the people betting on it expect it never to ship under that name. On Manifold, a forecasting site that trades with play money, the market "When will Meta release Llama 5?" already resolved No. The article says it also explains how the Llama line turned into Muse and how likely a model with that name is to ship at all. The article leaves open which Muse Spark version the open checkpoint matches. The article does not say what Meta plans to release next under the Muse name.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia head amid infidelity and chip export restriction allegations
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the head of Nvidia after thirty three years of leadership. He admitted to infidelity with a woman running an Asian chip supply company called Megaspeed. This personal relationship coincided with accusations that Huang bypassed American export restrictions on advanced computing chips. The controversy gained credibility after a major newspaper reported the details of the situation. These events occurred around November 2026 while Nvidia employed nearly 50,000 people worldwide.

The situation involved Megaspeed purchasing at least 4.8 billion dollars of Nvidia hardware. Trump approved further chip sales to China for a reported 25 percent payment to the government. Nvidia contributed 25 million dollars to a ballroom project benefiting the president and his contractors. Trump held a personal Nvidia investment valued between 13 million and 62 million dollars. Howard Lutnick led the Commerce Department, which had the authority to blacklist the company Megaspeed.

Howard Lutnick boasted that he promised Huang easy access to the president of the United States. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Lutnick for delaying the restrictions on chip sales to China. Donald Trump stated that the country is stronger and that America plays games with China. Huang argued that selling chips to everyone, including China, would strengthen American technological leadership. Trump expressed support for Huang returning, suggesting that the executive had learned a big lesson.

Elon Musk and 180,000 other technology executives, workers, and shareholders signed a petition for Huang's reinstatement. Former NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder said blaming Lutnick spares the president and the silent principals. Many employees in Santa Clara, California, became millionaires through generous stock awards and compensation. Many other workers face displacement and uncertainty as the AI revolution concentrates wealth among infrastructure owners. The existing leadership at Nvidia remains uncertain about whether they should reinstate the former chief executive.

Nvidia began as a gaming chipmaker and reached a market capitalisation approaching 4.8 trillion dollars. Fiscal 2026 revenue reportedly reached 216 billion dollars before the resignation of the founder. Huang arrived from Taiwan at age nine and studied at Oregon State and Stanford universities. The company launched a 500 billion dollar financing platform for AI start ups and cloud providers. US intelligence agencies suspected Megaspeed was connected to the intelligence apparatus of the Beijing government.

Democrats may start congressional investigations after the new Congress takes office on January 3. A probe into illegal sales reportedly stalled after Jeff Kessler allegedly tipped off the company. This market entry prompted analysts to compare the new company to Meta Platforms, as both entities hold a market capitalization of approximately 1.5 trillion dollars. While both firms are heavily invested in artificial intelligence, Meta possesses a massive social media advertising business that provides a financial safety net. This existing revenue stream allows Meta to remain stable even if the broader artificial intelligence investment trend fails.

The company reported that its advertising revenue grew by 26 percent in the third quarter, significantly outpacing the 12 percent growth seen at Pinterest. Meta expects fourth quarter revenue to reach between 73 billion and 76 billion dollars, representing a growth rate of 22 to 27 percent. However, capital expenditures of 34.9 billion dollars exceeded the operating cash flow of 32.8 billion dollars during the third quarter. Management has provided a guidance for 2026 capital expenditures ranging from 135 billion to 145 billion dollars. As of September 30, the company held 454.5 billion dollars in commitments that cannot be canceled.

Dan Niles, the founder of Niles Investment Management, stated that Meta has a social media business that generates a ton of cash. He argued that this diversification gives Meta a distinct advantage over Anthropic, which lacks a secondary revenue source. Mike Santoli of CNBC also noted the similar market valuations of the two companies during a November 18 broadcast. Meta management believes that upgrades to ad ranking models are driving better conversions and justifying the heavy spending on compute. These leaders suggest that the current investments in artificial intelligence are already providing tangible benefits to the advertising engine.

The current financial situation creates risks for suppliers like Arista Networks, which saw third quarter revenue jump 58.5 percent to 3.66 billion dollars. Because Microsoft and Meta accounted for 42 percent of Arista's 2025 revenue, any reduction in Meta's spending would hit the supplier first. Investors are currently paying about 19 times forward earnings for Meta, which is below its five year average of 21 times. The market will look for more clarity during the fourth quarter earnings call in late January. Analysts expect total capital expenditures for 2027 to be roughly 210 billion dollars.

stories.Headline: Developer mjwsolo releases open source Localcode for agentic coding on Mac computers
stories.Summary:

This open source tool allows users to install the system with one command and run it within their own projects. The software can read and edit files, run tests, execute shell commands, and search code by structure or content. It also scaffolds and launches applications while remembering specific tasks across multiple messages.

The system requires a Mac with Apple Silicon running macOS 13 or newer and at least 16 GB of unified memory. Users must have Python 3.10 or newer and enough disk space for the software and one of 12 available models. These models, which include options like Gemma 4 and DeepSeek V4 Flash, offer 169 different quantization options and download from Hugging Face. The largest model download reaches 161.9 GB, while the smallest is 4.7 GB.

The creator of Localcode stated that powerful and personal artificial intelligence should work for everyone on any device and anywhere. This philosophy led to the decision to make the inference process local rather than cloud based. The developer claims that Localcode represents a first step toward achieving this goal of accessible local AI. Most operations remain offline, although the network is used for model downloads and specific web tools.

The system requires a Windows PC with a graphics card and Unsloth Desktop. James used an RTX 5090 with 32GB VRAM to run Qwen3.8-27B with 4-bit quantization. Jerry James is responsible for the guide and the specific hardware configuration. He stated that cloud providers act like appliance businesses for routine tasks. He claimed that OpenAI and Anthropic drop model quality in their latest versions. James said he wanted to avoid usage limits for research and coding tasks. He chose Unsloth Desktop because he liked the name and lacked subscriptions.

The author claims that cloud experiences are convenient but have ballooning costs. He notes that privacy concerns make moving to local hardware a good case. Users with different VRAM capacities are affected by which models they can run. Those with 8 to 12GB VRAM can handle smaller 9B to 12B models. People with 32GB VRAM can comfortably run 27B to 35B models.

Quantization shrinks models by compressing weights to fit on consumer graphics cards. This process trades some accuracy for faster speeds and lower memory usage. Mixture of experts models run only a few billion parameters for each token. Unified memory on Macs or specific PCs allows for larger model sizes. Inkling 2 Small is a 594B model requiring a 256GB Mac Studio.

Users can now share their local AI via the LAN access setting. They must set a remote password and share the provided network address. The PC must remain on for other home users to access it. Anthropic faced a Pentagon dispute and a race with OpenAI while securing nearly 900 billion dollars in compute contracts. stories.Headline: ModelBest expands international AI access through an efficiency-first strategy
stories.Summary:
ModelBest expanded its international access to artificial intelligence technology by focusing on efficiency during a keynote speech delivered by CEO Li Dahai. This event took place at the Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal, which was held from November 9 to 12. According to a report from China Daily, the company used an efficiency-first strategy to make intelligence more inclusive and widely deployable. By November, the self-developed MiniCPM series of models had recorded more than 70 million downloads worldwide.

The strategy requires high intelligence density and lower costs on devices rather than relying on massive computing power. In April, ModelBest revealed LaoAI, which is a national model for Laos built on the MiniCPM architecture and high-efficiency training methods. This system is integrated into the national government communications platform known as G-Chat v2 and is used across key industries. ModelBest delivered the complete model weights and application programming interfaces to local developers to give Laos control over the data.

CEO Li Dahai stated that efficiency is the key to making large model technology available to everyone. He claimed that an 8-billion-parameter system achieved world-leading Lao-language capability, proving that developing countries do not need top-tier computing power. Li Dahai also said that using AI to build AI represents a fundamental shift in how intelligence is produced. He noted that the MiniCPM family of models serves different forms of intelligence while maintaining faster speeds.

The company claims its on-device approach allows small businesses to possess AI capability without cloud capacity or per-inference fees. This direction follows the 2026 Government Work Report of China, which endorsed open-source AI ecosystems. ModelBest aims to share Chinese AI advancements so that nations in the Global South can develop capabilities in their own languages. The company intends to continue prioritizing efficiency and openness to reach countries and businesses that have been waiting on the sidelines.

This structure affected 65 percent of the S&P 500 including utilities and banks.

Steve Eisman is a longtime investor and the host of the Weekly Wrap. He said the Jensen unwind is just starting and will get very ugly. Investors in the S&P 500 are impacted because info tech is about 40 percent. Tech-adjacent names like Google and Amazon bring that total to roughly 50 percent. stories.Headline: Meta pauses business terms on web crawling after publisher backlash
stories.Summary:
Meta has paused proposed business terms that alarmed publishing groups over the possible crawling of websites tied to business accounts, the company said, after Nieman Lab reported on the backlash to the language. The company said it is now collecting feedback from stakeholders and intends to discuss revised terms with publishers and regulators in early 2027 before putting anything into effect. It said the pause followed concerns raised about its web crawlers and noted that it honors the industry-standard robots.txt protocol, which lets sites signal their crawling preferences. The retreat comes as the traffic and advertising economics that have long sustained the media business come under strain from AI-powered search and chatbots, which can answer questions directly instead of sending readers to publishers' pages.

Google said its News AI pilot now covers more than 400 publishers worldwide, including Axios, CNN and the Financial Times, with the company paying participating outlets to license material for specific Google News features such as article overviews and personalized audio briefings. Google is separately testing a broader model that compensates publishers according to how much their content contributes to AI-generated answers across Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Anthropic signed a licensing agreement with the Associated Press covering real-time election information inside Claude, its first publisher licensing deal. In court documents made public in unsealed filings, OpenAI's head of ChatGPT, Nick Turley, acknowledged that AI products were largely substitutive of publishers' work and represented an existential threat to their businesses, and the same filings showed that OpenAI president Greg Brockman replied with a short approving remark when an employee described a workaround for the New York Times paywall.

Publishers have watched referral traffic from search and social platforms become less dependable, and generative tools threaten to compress it further by summarizing reporting without a click, which has pushed trade groups and individual outlets to press for licensing fees, crawl controls and clearer rules on attribution. For the AI companies, licensing deals give them defensible access to fresh, authoritative material and reduce legal exposure as copyright litigation advances, but each concession raises the cost of training and serving models, and a contribution-based payment model as Google is testing could prove harder to administer at scale than flat licensing fees. The Meta episode shows how quickly proposed terms can become a public fight, and pausing the language buys the company time, but the 2027 timeline means publishers will spend another year without clarity on how their sites may be accessed. Apple, for its part, is hiring to build an agentic AI assistant capable of browsing sites autonomously, moving across apps, generating and debugging code and connecting to outside services, a reminder that the demand for machine-readable content is only going to grow.

stories.Headline: Anthropic ports AI models to AMD chips in days without engineers
stories.Summary:
Anthropic disclosed that its Claude Mythos model can move part of its AI workloads onto non-Nvidia chips in just a few days with basically no human intervention, a job that used to take six to 12 months and dozens of engineers. The disclosures came as Anthropic prepares for its IPO, and the headline capability is software that rewrites and tunes AI models to run on different hardware largely on its own. The specific benchmark is AMD's MI355X GPUs, which Claude Mythos can port an AI model to in approximately three days compared to the old norm of 6-12 months. Nvidia's dominance has never rested on silicon alone, because its CUDA software ecosystem is the real lock-in that developers built their tools around. Anthropic's deal for AMD's Instinct GPUs is projected to reach multi-gigawatt scale, with the first phase set for the first half of 2027.

AMD reportedly offers a per-gigawatt system cost that is roughly half that of some Nvidia platforms, and Nvidia's share of contracted future AI compute capacity for frontier labs has declined to around 39% from previous highs of 80% or more. Alphabet stands to benefit because its tensor processing units, or TPUs, are custom chips built for AI workloads that gain when customers can move models onto them without a costly rewrite. TSMC may be the quietest beneficiary, since it manufactures chips for Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom and collects revenue no matter which designer wins the procurement fight. For Nvidia, the risk is less about losing sales tomorrow and more about losing pricing power over time, with the 39% capacity share figure the number to watch.

For AMD, the opportunity is direct, because its biggest obstacle was software friction rather than chip performance, and the Anthropic deal becomes a proof of concept other buyers can point to. The articles note risks to the commoditization story, since Anthropic's results cover part of its workloads rather than all of them, and porting a model is different from running it at peak efficiency across every task. Nvidia also still holds a large installed base and deep relationships with nearly every major AI buyer, while overall demand for AI chips continues to look strong as companies spread purchases across vendors. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Greg Abel oversees Berkshire Hathaway's 367 billion dollar portfolio with 30.2 percent in AI stocks
stories.Summary:

He analyzed how the company manages its large portfolio under the leadership of CEO Greg Abel. The report focuses on the firm's significant exposure to the artificial intelligence sector through specific stocks. It examines the current distribution of assets within a total portfolio valued at 367 billion dollars. The author evaluates which technology investments align best with the long term philosophy of Warren Buffett.

The portfolio holds 30.2 percent of its value in Apple and Alphabet, which are both artificial intelligence stocks. Large language models like ChatGPT present challenges to the business model of Alphabet by competing with Google Search services. Investors prioritizing business durability over speculative upside may find Apple more aligned with the preference for established, enduring franchises. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead the fiscal 2027 third quarter earnings report after the market closes November 17. Constellation Energy has power agreements with Amazon for 690 megawatts and with Alphabet for about 890 megawatts.

stories.Headline: Claude AI predicts Chainlink could fall to $1.85 by January 2027 in a bearish scenario
stories.Summary:
Anthropic's Claude AI predicted that Chainlink faces a catastrophic collapse that could erase years of progress and leave the token trading at a fraction of its former relevance by the first day of 2027, according to a TradingView article published on November 21, 2026. The hypothetical landmark catalyst in the prediction is a coordinated institutional rejection of decentralized oracles, in which a consortium of major global banks, clearing houses and rating agencies announces in mid-2027 that it will migrate all critical data feeds, cross-chain messaging and compliance infrastructure to a new permissioned, bank-operated oracle network built on proprietary technology. The article says the consortium cites unresolved concerns around decentralization risks, potential single points of failure in the broader ecosystem and regulatory pressure for fully controllable systems, and that it effectively freezes new production deployments of Chainlink's CCIP and Data Streams. Existing pilots are wound down, and the narrative that Chainlink would become the standard connective tissue for tokenized finance collapses almost overnight, the article says.

In this extreme but not impossible scenario, Claude AI predicts that Chainlink could trade at $1.85 by January 1, 2027, which the article describes as a probability-weighted bearish scenario rather than a certainty. On higher-timeframe charts looking into 2027, the article says LINK has spent years forming a broad distribution pattern after its previous-cycle peak, with multi-year descending trendlines and failed attempts to sustain higher structural highs leaving the asset vulnerable to a decisive breakdown. Should the institutional narrative fracture, measured-move projections from the long-term range and Fibonacci extensions of prior major declines open the door to a deep retracement of the entire post-2020 advance, and volume profiles and long-term moving-average clusters that once acted as support would flip into heavy overhead supply. The article says macro conditions, liquidity and risk appetite will ultimately determine the path.

The article notes that recent catalysts widely viewed as bullish could kill the Claude prediction, including high-profile integrations Chainlink secured throughout late 2026, expanded CCIP volume metrics and a completed Moody's testnet pilot for multi-chain credit ratings. It also partnered with OpenZeppelin for institutional tooling, advanced work with LG CNS on Korean digital assets, and saw banks publicly discuss moving from exploration into production systems. However, the article says that if these announcements ultimately fail to convert into sticky, high-volume, fee-generating usage that meaningfully accrues value to the LINK token, they risk becoming evidence of over-promised institutional adoption. A sudden pivot by the same institutions toward closed alternatives would turn the current partnership pipeline into a liability rather than an asset, according to the article.

stories.Headline: Nvidia's 40% slide spreads AI bubble fears to stocks and Bitcoin
stories.Summary:
Nvidia shares fell roughly 40% from their October 6, 2026 all-time closing high of $243.37 to around $150 by mid-November, and the selloff spread to the S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the crypto market. Bitcoin traded below $60,000 on November 21, 2026, with an intraday low somewhere between $55,000 and $57,000, and the asset has now fallen more than 30% since September 2026. The total crypto market contracted to approximately $2 trillion, down from a peak above $4 trillion in October 2025, while the S&P 500 entered correction territory with weekly losses exceeding 8% as of November 21, 2026. The Dow also slipped into a correction, and both benchmarks now sit more than 10% below their recent peaks, according to Crypto Briefing.

The anxiety centers on whether the trillions of dollars flowing into AI infrastructure will ever earn back what they cost, since AI infrastructure spending is projected at $7 trillion through 2030 while Gartner forecasts AI revenue over the same window at only $3.6 trillion. Nvidia sells the chips that power data centers, so if the companies buying those chips start doubting the payoff, they may slow their orders. The selling pressure on Bitcoin appears to reflect a broad, macro-driven liquidity squeeze rather than any problem specific to crypto, and no major exchange failure or protocol exploit is behind the move. Instead, Bitcoin is trading like a high-beta risk asset that moves with tech stocks, so when investors pull money out of speculative growth bets, digital assets tend to get swept up in the same tide.

The article was written by Diego Almada Lopez and edited by him, and it states that the gap between projected AI spending and forecast revenue is unlikely to close quickly, calling a $7 trillion capex bill against $3.6 trillion in expected revenue a structural mismatch rather than a quarterly blip. It says each new earnings report from chipmakers and cloud providers will be read as evidence for or against the bubble thesis. For crypto traders, the key signal may sit outside crypto entirely, because as long as Bitcoin trades in step with the Nasdaq and the S&P 500, the path of the AI trade could help set the direction for digital assets too. The article carries a disclosure that all content is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice.

stories.Headline: Hancom launches Nomadian AI workforce platform in the US and pursues AWS Marketplace listing
stories.Summary:
South Korea's Hancom has begun commercializing Nomadian, an AI workforce platform in which AI agents carry out corporate tasks, in the US market, the company said on Nov. 23. Hancom held a presentation on its US commercialization strategy for Nomadian at the Crowne Plaza hotel in Seattle on Nov. 16 local time and spent two days discussing cooperation with Amazon Web Services. The event drew Eugene Kawamoto, AWS director of Amazon Bedrock and AI go-to-market, along with partners including VisualFeast, ClickIt and TaskUs, as well as local media. Hancom also hired Bill Fanning as senior vice president and head of US business development for Nomadian, and he will oversee business development at the US subsidiary Hancom is in the process of establishing.

Nomadian is built on Amazon Bedrock, AWS's fully managed generative AI service, and Hancom is pursuing a listing on AWS Marketplace as well as indirect sales through managed service providers. In a 3D virtual office, users can build an organization by deploying Ara, an AI team leader, and 11 AI team members assigned by role and responsibility, and when a task is assigned, Ara divides the work among team members for market and competitor research, marketing content creation and sales proposal writing. Users can check progress and review and edit reports and proposals produced with Hancom's 36 years of accumulated core document technology, and the AI team learns the user's working style over time. Hancom plans to release a beta version in December and a global commercial version next March, targeting 10,000 user companies each month from December through February, up to 30,000 in total, and 10 to 15 local partners by next March.

Fanning pitched the ability to build and run an organization with AI before hiring actual employees as Nomadian's core competitive edge, saying the idea is to hand tasks such as customer response and project planning to an AI team so founders can focus on growing the business. He said what the company is strategically focused on right now is the partnership with AWS, and that based on Hancom's organizational foundation and capabilities he will make sure Nomadian delivers results quickly in the US. Hancom aims to secure partners including the US Small Business Development Center, startup mentoring group SCORE, accelerators and university startup centers, with a goal of 3 to 5 network partners before the beta launches in December. It will select 500 beta companies with the best results as "Nomadian 500," supporting them with prize money and mentoring, and will run advertising in major US cities to recruit beta waitlist members.

Hancom held a separate session with AWS working-level staff and met Mark Relph, AWS director of data and AI partners, on Nov. 17 to discuss commercialization strategy. Once listed on AWS Marketplace, AWS customers will be able to subscribe to Nomadian through their existing accounts, and Hancom is also considering an indirect sales model in which managed service providers bundle Nomadian with their own services. The pricing system is being designed to reflect AI workload while letting customers predict costs, and Hancom plans to refine the pricing based on usage data gathered during the beta and apply it to the commercial service next March. The company cites the rapid growth of solo entrepreneurs and small operators in the US as another reason for the market opportunity, and it expects that as more small businesses use AI, Nomadian's potential customer base will grow with them.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prices IPO above range and lists on Nasdaq at $111.50
stories.Summary:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, and began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, listing at $111.50, Yahoo Finance reported on Saturday, November 21, 2026. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, praised Anthropic's AI models ahead of the Nasdaq debut, saying he had met members of the team before SpaceX agreed to supply computing capacity. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reiterated that his company is a "big believer" in Anthropic ahead of its Nasdaq debut. Anthropic's landmark IPO put the AI company's relationships with some of the biggest technology companies in focus that week. The company's filing identifies Amazon, Google and Microsoft as companies that "develop and deploy competing AI models."

Anthropic's IPO filing says it expects to pay SpaceX about $3.1 billion a month once all the promised computing capacity is delivered. Musk said Anthropic is "extremely likely" to keep renting computing capacity from SpaceX and could seek another 10 gigawatts. Amazon is set to hold roughly 14.7% of Anthropic's capital stock after the IPO and concurrent private placement, while Alphabet's Google will own about 13.7%, according to the company's filing. Together, the two companies will hold roughly 28.4%. Anthropic has committed to spend between $47.2 billion and $49.2 billion with Microsoft, and Google agreed to purchase $10 billion in non-voting Anthropic stock through the private placement.

Musk said "Opus and Fable are great products" and that "no one I know at Anthropic set off my evil detector." He described Anthropic's executives as "principled" and "diligent," and called the potential additional 10 gigawatts a "big number." Musk cautioned that demand could decline in a "worst-case scenario" if governments impose severe restrictions on AI, and said the agreements are short-term and either side can terminate them. He added that he would end the arrangement if he believed Anthropic was doing something "really terrible for the world."

Jassy said "we're big believers in Anthropic" and has previously said customers want access to multiple leading AI models, a dynamic that benefits Amazon Web Services by allowing it to offer third-party models such as Anthropic's Claude. Beyond Musk and Jassy, the other Magnificent Seven CEOs did not make new public comments specifically addressing Anthropic or its IPO during the week, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, Nvidia's Colette Kress, Apple CEO Tim Cook and Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg. Retail sentiment around AMZN stock stayed in 'bearish' territory over the past week, accompanied by 'low' levels of chatter. Retail sentiment around ANT stock stayed in 'extremely bullish' territory through the week, with chatter at 'extremely high' levels.

Amazon, Alphabet's Google and Nvidia are among Anthropic's investors, while Microsoft is a major financial backer and infrastructure partner. SpaceX, led by Tesla CEO Elon Musk, is also supplying computing capacity to the Claude developer. Musk said he knew several Anthropic employees from his time at OpenAI. Microsoft participated in Anthropic's private placement, adding to its financial and commercial relationship with the AI company. Musk said the SpaceX agreements are short-term and either side can terminate them, and that he would end the arrangement if he believed Anthropic was doing something "really terrible for the world." stories.Headline: Mark Gurman reports Apple Siri layoffs hit older infrastructure while annual release cycle limits AI response
stories.Summary:
Apple's recent Siri layoffs affected employees working on the assistant's older infrastructure rather than its newer AI systems, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Gurman reported the layoffs in his latest "Power On" newsletter, published on Sunday, November 22, 2026. The MacRumors article carrying his report was published that day at 12:29 pm PST and written by Hartley Charlton. Gurman said employees have yet to notice a major difference in how Apple operates despite efforts to accelerate development. He added that Apple faces growing competition from AI developers that update their models and services far more frequently than Apple's annual operating system cycle.

Within software engineering chief Craig Federighi's organization, Apple follows an internal release calendar labeled A through G, with engineering work tied to specific software versions and launch windows. Depending on the release, the roadmap and features for a major operating system update are largely determined by late summer or early fall of the preceding year. Gurman argued that this structure leaves Apple with limited flexibility to respond to competitors' breakthroughs during the subsequent development cycle. Siri's multistep control of Apple apps is expected to launch in December, with third-party app support following in 2027. Apple is reportedly developing a more advanced AI agent, but Gurman does not expect it to arrive before late 2027.

Gurman criticized Siri's slow responses, limited third-party integration, and seemingly worsening dictation. He warned that rival agents could become difficult to abandon as they accumulate users' preferences and connected accounts. He said Apple's reputation for privacy and deeper platform access could help it compete. Gurman said employees have yet to notice a major difference in how Apple operates despite efforts to accelerate development and spread significant releases throughout the year. He argued the release calendar structure leaves Apple with limited flexibility to respond to competitors' breakthroughs.

Commenters on the MacRumors article responded to Gurman's report, with one saying agile software development is dead. Another commenter said it is ironic to suggest Apple prioritizes responding at all and argued Apple seems content to cede the AI space completely. A third commenter said the only way around this is to decouple Siri AI from operating system releases, as Google can update its apps without waiting for major versions. Another commenter said Apple already does six or seven significant releases throughout the year and that what Gurman asks for would mean substantially less planning and work on the software. One commenter said Apple's releases are largely tied to hardware launches and that competing would require restructuring teams, governance and ways of working.

Gurman's report appeared in his "Power On" newsletter for Bloomberg. MacRumors' guide lists iOS 27.2 features as including Siri AI improvements, Suggestions in Messages, and an Apple Music rebrand. The article's tags include Bloomberg, Mark Gurman, Siri Guide and Siri AI. The report follows Apple's efforts to accelerate development and spread significant releases throughout the year. Apple follows its internal A through G release calendar within Federighi's organization.

Siri's multistep control of Apple apps is expected to launch in December, with third-party app support following in 2027. Gurman does not expect Apple's more advanced AI agent to arrive before late 2027. The articles leave open which employees were laid off and how many. stories.Headline: Meta halts buybacks and borrows to fund AI data center spending
stories.Summary:
Meta stopped buying back its own stock, spending nothing on buybacks in the first nine months of 2026 after spending $26 billion in the same period of 2025, and moved that cash into capital spending such as data centers. In those nine months its business brought in $97 billion, which was $17 billion more than a year earlier, and it put $83 billion into capital spending, or 86 cents of every dollar, up from 61 cents. Meta also borrowed $25 billion, lifting its debt from $29 billion a year earlier to $84 billion, and in November it sold another $15 billion and €9 billion of bonds. In late October it sold about $14 billion of preferred stock that converts into shares, and it agreed to sell 40 million new shares by November 2027. Its interest bill more than tripled to $2.3 billion, which the article says is still small next to the $97 billion of cash its business brought in.

Analysts expect Meta's sales to reach $313 billion in 2027, and at 55 cents of cash per $1 of sales that would bring in about $172 billion, leaving $167 billion to spend from its own cash after about $5 billion of dividends. Against its current spending pace of $136 billion, that leaves room to spend about $31 billion more without new debt, or about 23%, assuming no buybacks. Its room to borrow is the smallest of the three cash-rich buyers, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta, because its debt nearly tripled in the past year, and the November bonds cut that room to about $64 billion. Meta's $31 billion of room is worth about $16 billion to Nvidia, or up to about $63 billion if Meta borrows, since Nvidia's sales equal about 52 cents of every $1 the five biggest buyers spend.

The article says Meta traded its buybacks for data centers and also borrowed and sold stock on top, so its owners now carry more debt, with more shares on the way and no buybacks for now. If 2027 spending stays within the $167 billion Meta can pay from its own cash, buybacks could come back. On Friday, Nov 20, AI stocks had a hard day, with Nvidia falling 14.0%, the Nasdaq 100 fund 5.7%, Meta 5.9% and the S&P 500 fund 3.6%. The article also says about $118 billion of analysts' forecast for Nvidia is not yet covered by any buyer's cash or borrowing room.

stories.Headline: Microsoft AI chief Suleyman calls recursive self-improvement dangerous yet keeps deploying agents
stories.Summary:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman expressed deep nervousness about AI models improving other models. He spoke about this dangerous capability during a November 17 interview with Deirdre Bosa. This conversation occurred the same day Microsoft announced six new MAI models at Ignite. Suleyman described the last three months as a total watershed moment for the industry. He believes that recursive self-improvement is a very serious and dangerous capability.

Microsoft is putting AI agents on Windows 11 PCs and within Microsoft 365. The company announced seven new MAI models, including MAI Code 2 and MAI Cyber 2 Flash. A new contract in October 2025 allowed Microsoft to pursue AGI independently from OpenAI. The superintelligence team started 12 months ago to reach the absolute frontier next year. Microsoft Execution Containers became generally available on Windows 11 in October to provide guardrails.

Mustafa Suleyman said that models are now fully involved in improving the models that follow. He stated that the industry is not being alarmist about these recursive self-improvement risks. Suleyman believes that models must be proven safe step by step before entering production. He argued that Microsoft must ensure models are contained, aligned, and secured for users. He also stated that he is a humanist who strongly opposes the idea of handoverism.

John Langford, a 14 year veteran, quit Microsoft AI because the philosophy is scaling. Some Microsoft engineers admit the company cares more about winning than about product polish. Regular users are affected by agents that can organize, move, and rename their files. These agents may hallucinate or fall for attacks like cross-prompt injection on Windows PCs. Nation state grade capabilities could be available to the general public within six months.

Microsoft previously relied on OpenAI models served on Azure and wrapped inside the Copilot app. The company now uses gigawatts of compute to build its own frontier model ecosystem. A July breach at Hugging Face showed an autonomous AI agent breaking into production infrastructure. Suleyman previously wrote a book called The Coming Wave which pleaded for AI containment. He once told Axios that governments should license powerful AI to avoid acting too late.

Microsoft will continue rolling out MAI Code 2 into the GitHub Copilot platform now. The company has no plans to do open weight for its new frontier models. Suleyman wants AI labs to coordinate and share safety practices like the drug industry. He admitted that Microsoft has not hit the brakes on any technology so far. The articles leave open whether Microsoft will actually stop a model if it is dangerous.

Investors are increasingly expecting the Federal Reserve to raise rates again in December.

stories.Headline: Vietnam businesses adopt AI faster but few integrate it into operations
stories.Summary:
Vietnam’s adoption of artificial intelligence is rising among enterprises, but its integration into business operations remains limited because of barriers in workforce skills, data and organisational capacity, experts said, according to a report published by Asia News Network on November 23, 2026. The International Labour Organization said about 11.5 million jobs in Vietnam, equal to 20.8 per cent of total employment, were potentially affected by generative AI in 2024. The Vietnam Private Economic Report 2025, released earlier in the year by the Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry, included a survey on AI adoption in the workplace. Citing that survey, Dr Luong Minh Huan, director of the chamber’s Enterprise Development Institute, said AI adoption among private enterprises remains at an early stage. Of more than 3,500 private enterprises surveyed, 76.2 per cent have no AI use, 12.5 per cent use AI at a low level, 8.8 per cent report moderate use and 2.5 per cent use AI at a high level.

A study titled Unlocking Vietnam’s AI Potential 2026, released in September at Amazon Web Services Cloud and AI Day Hanoi, found that 26 per cent of Vietnamese businesses, or around 245,000 enterprises, had adopted AI, up from 18 per cent in 2025. Among those that had adopted AI, about 61 per cent were still experimenting, 23 per cent had developed comprehensive AI strategies and only 8 per cent had integrated AI into their business processes. The International Labour Organization reported that an AI-enabled vision system recently introduced by Hanoi Industry Trading Investment JSC cut inspection time from 20 seconds to five seconds and raised defect-detection accuracy from 95 per cent to 99 per cent, with 10 workers replaced by three senior high-tech supervisors. An internal AI assistant at VietinBank helped reduce document search time by 95 per cent and the time needed to prepare meeting minutes by 70 per cent, according to a bank report, while Techcombank’s Joule AI assistant helped reduce requests for HR policy support by 28 per cent over three months. Huan said these cases do not represent the broader business community, and that more enterprises using AI does not necessarily mean AI is integrated into operations.

Do Ngoc Ha, an official from the National Statistics Office under the Ministry of Finance, said measurement is important for assessing AI efficiency at work, and that the national AI strategy sets a target for the AI economy to account for 6 per cent of GDP. He said Vietnam currently has no official comprehensive measurement of the overall picture of AI adoption and its impact, and that only a number of small-scale studies have been conducted so far. The National Statistics Office is conducting various surveys and creating opportunities to add questions on AI adoption to existing surveys on labour and businesses, he said. Ho Thi Kim Ngan, deputy head of the Labour Relations Department at the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour, suggested surveys of workers to capture their opinions and experiences with AI adoption, saying working hours may become longer and work intensity may increase, placing workers under greater stress and pressure. Nguyen Tien Huy, director general of the chamber’s Office for Sustainable Business Development, said AI adoption does not automatically lead to higher productivity, and that technology delivers results only when businesses identify the right problems, redesign workflows, standardise data, adjust management practices and prepare their workforce.

ILO Country Director for Vietnam Sinwon Park said the organization believes AI should be adopted in a human-centred way, with productivity gains going together with better jobs, respect for rights at work and opportunities for workers to learn and adapt. She said AI policy cannot be only about technology, and that labour laws, employment policies, occupational safety and health, social protection and international labour standards remain important as workplaces change.

stories.Headline: UKRI awards 20 Turing AI fellowships worth over £39m to researchers
stories.Summary:
UK Research and Innovation awarded 20 Turing AI fellowships backed by more than £39 million, EdTech Innovation Hub reported on 23 November 2026. Seventeen researchers will apply AI in fields from economic history to clean energy, the article said. Three others will move to UK universities to advance core AI research. The Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council is delivering the awards through two schemes. The article said the projects are backed by government funding.

The Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships give researchers three years to apply AI in their own fields. The five-year Turing AI Global Fellowships bring researchers from overseas to work on how AI systems learn and interpret language and social behavior. The 17 Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships began in October 2026. The three Global Fellowships start in 2027. UKRI is funding researchers to use AI to analyze more than a million handwritten wills, detect rare events in dark matter experiments and study underground conditions for cleaner energy projects.

At the London School of Economics and Political Science, Professor Neil Cummins will use AI to examine handwritten wills for evidence of how people lived and worked over centuries. The University of Oxford’s Professor Jocelyn Monroe will use the search for dark matter to develop AI systems that can identify exceptionally rare events. Dr Roisin Buckley at the University of Glasgow will develop AI tools to help researchers better understand underground and seabed conditions for energy and infrastructure projects. At King’s College London, Dr Thiago Sogo Bezerra will combine AI with new detector technology to improve neutrino measurements, with potential applications in nuclear reactor monitoring and safety. Professor Charlotte Deane, Executive Chair of EPSRC, said the fellowships would give outstanding researchers the freedom and support to push the boundaries of AI itself while also applying it in new ways across a wide range of disciplines.

Professor Jonathan May will move from the University of Southern California to the University of Edinburgh to study how AI interprets intent in language. Professor Denny Wu will move from New York University and the Flatiron Institute to Oxford to develop a mathematical basis for predicting how deep learning behaves at scale. Professor Roi Reichart will move from Technion, Israel Institute of Technology, to the University of Cambridge to study how AI models social interaction and emotion. UKRI says earlier fellows have helped train AI researchers, launch startups and shape policy. The article named the universities of Edinburgh, Oxford and Cambridge as hosts for the global fellows.

The article said the 20 fellowships support AI research and its application across disciplines at UK universities. It said the awards are backed by government funding and delivered by EPSRC through the Pioneer Interdisciplinary and Global schemes. It described the Pioneer fellowships as giving researchers three years to apply AI in their own fields. It described the Global fellowships as five-year awards bringing researchers from overseas. It said the three Global Fellowships start in 2027 and the 17 Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships began in October 2026.

The article did not say what funding individual fellows will receive or how the more than £39 million will be divided. It did not name the remaining fellows beyond the seven researchers it described. It did not give the dates on which the Global Fellows will take up their posts in 2027. It did not say which overseas institutions beyond those named will send fellows. It did not say what happens after the three-year and five-year fellowship periods end.

stories.Headline: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang warns against handing control to AI systems
stories.Summary:
Alexandr Wang, Meta’s Chief AI Officer, posted a warning on November 22, 2026, that society should not hand over control to artificial intelligence systems, an unusual message from an executive whose job is to build them. He tied the warning to AI helping to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a long-standing mathematics problem about prime numbers, and said that milestone shows how fast AI capabilities are moving. When software starts contributing to frontier math, he argued, the “someday” timeline for superintelligence gets noticeably shorter. His core concern is control, and he warned that humans may struggle to keep authority over AI systems that are 1,000 times more capable than people.

Wang’s prescription is not to stop building, and he called for intentional choices in AI development that prioritize empowering humans rather than letting machine intelligence outrun human control. He became Meta’s Chief AI Officer in June 2025, after Meta acquired a 49% stake in his startup, Scale AI, for $14.3 billion. Meta’s capital expenditures on AI reached $72.2 billion in 2025, and the company has planned spending of between $115 billion and $135 billion for 2026. Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent app, in September 2026, and the launch resulted in nearly a 20% increase in Meta’s stock value.

Wang has not limited himself to posts, and he has restructured teams at Meta Superintelligence Labs to focus on human agency and safety as AI systems become extremely powerful. His concerns echo similar warnings from leaders at OpenAI, and the people building the most advanced systems are increasingly the ones publicly flagging the risks of those systems. For investors, the warning complicates a simple story, because Meta has been rewarded for shipping ambitious AI products, as the Muse-driven stock jump showed, and now its AI chief is publicly drawing a line between AI that empowers people and AI that replaces their judgment. Spending is the other variable to watch, with 2026 capital expenditures planned in the $115 billion to $135 billion range, and Wang’s specific claim that humans may struggle to manage systems 1,000 times more capable than themselves is a hedge, not a certainty.
