stories.Headline: A translator and technical writer lists eight AI terms for readers beyond tokens and prompts
stories.Summary:
The article lists eight AI terms it says are worth knowing beyond tokens, prompts and hallucinations, and it was published by eu.36kr.com on 2026-11-22 at 06:00:00Z. It was written by Shenyi Translation, a translation and compilation team under 36Kr that covers technology, business, workplace and life and introduces foreign technologies, perspectives and trends. The author says they are an AI enthusiast and technical writer who has created AI-related content for more than 5 years. They say they recently read an article titled “Master These 5 AI Terms and You Will Outperform 90% of People” and were familiar with all five terms in it. They say they wrote this article to share 8 more terms in plain language without piling up obscure technical jargon.

The article says a native large language model is like a brain in a jar that cannot open Slack, send emails or know when to stop on its own. It says the Harness is software wrapped around the model that lets it call tools, read information, manage permissions, control retry logic and termination conditions, and ask for help when needed. It says code agents are an example, with the Harness providing tools to read files, edit code and run tests while managing instructions and feedback to the model. It says two applications using the same base large model can perform very differently because their Harness opens different tools, instructions and result verification methods. It says Agents can perform operations step by step, call tools and complete a task independently, giving a refund example in which the agent finds the order, checks the refund policy, drafts the application and asks for approval before submission.

The article says the basic agent workflow is to plan actions, perform operations, verify results and decide what to do next. It says an agent is like an assistant with a to-do list authorized to use specific software, and that the upper limit of tasks depends on available tools and permissions. It says an agent that can only browse web pages is completely different from one connected to your email, files and calendar. It says you must confirm what content an agent can access, what information it can modify and when it needs your approval. It says MCP can basically be understood as the USB-C interface in the AI field, providing a unified standard for AI applications to connect to tools and data sources.

The article says that without a unified standard developers often need separate docking programs for each AI application, but with MCP one set of connections can be reused by multiple compatible applications. It says the MCP server opens specific tools or data to AI applications, for example letting AI assistants retrieve internal company documents or create new work orders in project management tools. It says configuration is still required, the AI application itself must support the protocol and you must grant corresponding access permissions. It says if a product claims to support MCP you can pay attention to what services it can connect to and what operations the assistant can perform through the protocol. It says most agent work follows a loop pattern of selecting an action, performing it, checking the result and retrying if it fails, and that a code agent may modify files, run tests, read error messages and adjust the code.

The article says this loop may go wrong, with the agent repeatedly performing invalid operations or stopping early before the task is completed. It says Loop engineering refers to designing the operation rules of this loop, including how the agent receives feedback and judges whether to continue, and that it is an emerging direction in agent development. It lists questions the loop must answer, including to what extent a task is considered completed, the maximum number of retries, the maximum time and cost, when the agent should ask humans for help and who or what mechanism verifies results. It says you can require a code agent to pass specified tests before success or set it to stop after three consecutive failures and explain the cause. It says a Skill is a pre-saved execution process the agent can call directly when it encounters a matching task, with a reimbursement form example specifying which fields to fill in, how expenses are classified and what to do when receipts are missing.

The article says that in Anthropic's skill specification instructions are written in the SKILL.md file and the supporting package can include scripts, templates and reference documents. It says that in Claude you can add custom skills or template skills on the skills page, and that ChatGPT adds skills on the customization page. It says the agent at first only sees the name and introduction of a skill and loads the full detailed instructions when it judges the skill is needed. It says MCP opens up access to tools and data for agents while skills tell them how to use these tools to complete specific work, with a monthly sales report example. It says GEO relates to how your content can be retrieved and cited by AI agents, and that people now ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Google AI Summaries for answers and click links far less often.

The article says GEO, Generation Engine Optimization, aims to get your brand mentioned, your content cited and your products recommended when AI generates responses. It says AEO, Answer Engine Optimization, aims to make your content suitable for direct answer generation, including answer cards on search engines and Q&A content from AI assistants. It says the two concepts overlap and different companies do not have completely consistent classification standards for them. It says clear descriptions, accurate product information and reliable sources increase the probability of your content being cited, but even doing all these well does not guarantee the AI will mention you. It says Computer Use refers to an AI system's ability to interact with the screen by clicking, typing, scrolling pages and selecting content, following a process of taking a screenshot, determining the next action, clicking or typing and reading the screen again.

The article says ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Grok all support Computer Use, and that ChatGPT can enable this function in the integration menu under Settings. It says Computer Use is useful when an application does not open a suitable API interface, which is the channel for software to exchange information and execute instructions directly. It says that even if a booking service does not open a docking interface, the agent can still enter information in the booking form. It says Computer Use carries risks, as the agent may click the wrong button, misread the page or get stuck at a certain step, and that important operations such as order placement, submission and account information modification must be manually reviewed. It says AGI generally refers to AI that can reach the same level as humans in a wide range of intellectual tasks, including learning knowledge in unfamiliar fields, solving various different problems and transferring learned knowledge across domains.

The article says researchers have not yet reached a consensus on AGI's exact definition and evaluation criteria, and that Google DeepMind has a paper proposing judgment ideas from two dimensions, the breadth of system capabilities and task performance. It says Superintelligence goes a step further, with capabilities that significantly surpass humans in the vast majority of intellectual tasks. It says AI that is only good at a single task cannot be counted as either, and that even a model that writes excellent code and solves complex math problems may perform very poorly in other things. It says when companies mention these two terms in their promotions you should check their specific definitions and what capabilities the system has verified instead of only looking at the labels. It says that next time a vendor says their product is equipped with agents you can ask what specific tasks it can complete, and if it supports MCP you can check what applications it can connect to.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Netizens use AI to develop custom desktop pet software
stories.Summary:
Netizens have started developing custom desktop pet software using AI as these gadgets gain popularity again. This trend emerged recently and was reported by the author Guozi on November 23, 2026. Users are creating these tools to kill boredom rather than to improve their production efficiency. Many people are sharing their self-made cases on social media platforms like Douyin and Xiaohongshu. These creations allow people who do not understand code to get in touch with software development.

The process requires a desktop Agent like WorkBuddy to customize functions according to specific user needs. Guozi used this tool to package a minimalist workday motivator as a desktop plugin for Mac. Some users create pets using photos of their own animals or favorite cute anime girls. Others make pets from images of roommates or bosses to crawl on the desktop for fun. One user developed a tool called RememberPal to record solar and lunar calendar birthdays for Mac.

Guozi stated that the era of building tool applications from scratch has finally arrived for everyone. The author claimed that numbers can save those who are oppressed by numbers like KPI or OKR. Guozi noted that people are not afraid of hardship when they are doing things that are fun. The author mentioned that AI makes the world feel different for a code novice like himself. He explained that WorkBuddy provides 100 free points daily for users who log in every day.

Overworked office workers are affected by this trend and use these tools to motivate their daily work. Some users include fitness plans in their motivators because they are trained by bosses and clients. Others use animations of donkeys pulling mills to express the feeling of spinning in the same place. Some netizens make their tools look like antivirus software to hide how they are making money. People with trypophobia are advised to stay away from pets that look like crawling cockroaches.

The articles state that vibe coding desktop pets were popular for a while before the workday motivators. Independent developers previously focused on a three-piece set consisting of bookkeeping, diary, and to-do list tools. Google announced at the Google I/O 2026 conference that Google AI Studio now supports Android applications. Users can now input natural language to generate an Android APK installation package for mobile devices. This shift means that almost anyone can now customize their own basic bookkeeping or diary tools.

Users can now make simple application tools without downloading software or paying for expensive memberships. The articles leave open whether users have the motivation to spend time and energy using Agents. Complex apps that require servers or high concurrency still have very high thresholds for AI development. Guozi offered to share a dmg file for Mac users or an HTML file for Windows users. It remains to be seen how many people will move from funny tools to useful ones.

stories.Headline: MiniMax releases MIM model that solves Millennium Prize Problems and breaks cryptographic records
stories.Summary:
MiniMax released an internal model called MIM that broke global records in automated cryptanalysis on November 20, 2026. This AI system cracked multiple cryptographic puzzles and solved two Millennium Prize Problems. The model proved the Riemann Hypothesis and the Navier-Stokes equations. These achievements occurred on the same day. The Lean official team confirmed the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis proof.

The MIM model used a 64-core server to solve the TII McEliece challenge in 1.8 to 5.36 seconds. This speed was 6,180 to 43,400 times faster than a multi-GPU cluster used by Anthropic. For a lattice isomorphism problem, MIM used a single-core CPU to find a key in 30.9 minutes. Anthropic previously used a 96-core server for nearly four hours on this task. MIM also cracked the Waterfall-256 algorithm in 0.045 seconds.

MiniMax stated that Chinese teams are now competing in the AI for Science battlefield. The company released eight analysis reports with runnable code to prove these results. They claimed that cryptanalysis is a brutal testing ground for large models. The company highlighted that MIM converted high-order mathematical derivations into practical attack codes. This process demonstrated the ability of AI to carry out scientific exploration.

Anthropic engineers responded by reposting and liking the results of the MiniMax model. The AI affected the security boundaries of post-quantum cryptography candidate schemes like LOCKER-I and ROLLO-I. It also impacted the COLM algorithm, which had been published in the Journal of Cryptology. A known expert noted that cryptography tests are brutal because scripts either recover the key or they do not. The model also found a human error in the DRS signature verification logic.

The articles state that the TII McEliece challenge previously had an academic record of 9.2 hours. The NIST standardization competition serves as a primary benchmark for the cryptography community. ETH Zurich and Anthropic created CryptanalysisBench to test if models memorize training data. The LOCKER-I scheme previously required 42 PB of memory to construct a specific matrix. The COLM algorithm had won the CAESAR authenticated encryption competition after five years of selection.

MIM compressed the LOCKER-I matrix from 42 PB down to 58 MB. The model used a mod 2 sublattice to reduce a search from 118 dimensions to 80 dimensions. It forged a legitimate ciphertext for COLM0 using only two queries. The articles leave open how long other mathematical fortresses can resist such AI. They also leave open the future of algorithms that previously had no known practical attacks.

stories.Headline: CertiK and Columbia University researchers formally verify production AI operators from DeepSeek and FlashAttention
stories.Summary:
CertiK and Columbia University researchers announced TensorLean on November 20, 2026. This project achieved the first formal verification of multiple production-grade AI operators. The verified operators include those from DeepSeek and the FlashAttention library. This process uses mathematical proof to ensure that GPU code meets expectations. The team focused on verifying compiled PTX instructions rather than source code.

The project evaluated 149 compiled GPU kernel instances across different hardware generations. It covered DeepSeek's DeepGEMM and the FlashAttention operator library from versions two to four. The team found 38 correctness issues across six libraries, including 23 from FlashAttention. Two defects were found in DeepGEMM, and 66 total instances failed verification. These instances spanned the Ampere, Hopper, and Blackwell GPU architectures.

The researchers stated that traditional testing cannot find all possible errors in complex GPU kernels. They explained that TensorLean handles concurrency by using role-based classification and representative threads. To manage dynamicity, the team used loop invariant technology to cover all parameter combinations. They addressed floating-point precision by calculating the upper bound of accumulated rounding errors. The team also decoupled mathematical logic from memory layout to reduce specification costs.

The researchers noted that defects in FlashAttention could affect every model using it. This library is widely deployed in frameworks like PyTorch, vLLM, and SGLang. The team found a specific error in FlashAttention-4 that 17,760 tests on an H100 missed. This highlights how underlying computational errors can cause chaotic and unpredictable model outputs. Such failures could endanger safety in critical systems like autonomous driving.

The articles mention a previous reliability crisis involving the Claude large language model. In August 2025, some Claude users saw Thai text and syntax errors in English prompts. Anthropic explained that a runtime optimization for TPU servers caused these computational errors. This anomaly emerged on August 25 and was rolled back by September 2, 2025. These errors disrupted the model's normal probability distribution and undermined the user experience.

The team completed formal verification for 27 kernels related to DeepSeek. They also inspected 37 source code kernels from FlashAttention, totaling 102 compiled instances. The team wrote specifications for 72 open-source kernels using 10,278 lines of code. The articles do not state if the discovered defects have been fixed. It remains open whether this method will be applied to other AI operators.

stories.Headline: Anthropic warns of brainpower deflation as it prepares IPO with $1.26-1.41 trillion valuation
stories.Summary:
Anthropic warned on November 23, 2026, that there is no escaping brainpower deflation. The company faces a future where its endgame may resemble the AI version of Google or AT&T. This warning comes as the company prepares for its initial public offering. The firm is struggling with the burden of massive computing power contracts. These contracts total nearly 1 trillion US dollars on the balance sheet.

The IPO pricing puts the fully diluted valuation between 1.26 and 1.41 trillion US dollars. This range is about 16 to 17 times the October annual recurring revenue of 81 billion US dollars. Some calculations based on Q4 annualized revenue of 77 billion US dollars suggest a multiple of 18 times. The company previously saw a primary market valuation of 965 billion US dollars in May. IPO expectations once rose as high as 1.5 trillion US dollars.

Dolphin analyzed the value judgment of Anthropic and the growth prospects of AI. The analyst noted that revenue needs to rise 4 to 5 times to afford computing costs. Dolphin questioned if the intelligence premium can be sustained as token prices drop. The analyst also examined the total addressable market for AI large model applications. This study focuses on competitive barriers and the impact of intellectual deflation.

Optimistic investors like Gavin Baker and Brad Gerstner anchor the market at 40 trillion US dollars. They view the salaries of global knowledge workers as the total reachable market space. Bearish institutions instead link the target market to enterprise IT budgets of 6 trillion US dollars. These pessimists believe Anthropic will only get 3 percent of that budget in five years. This would result in 180 billion US dollars in revenue.

The articles state that global labor income is about 60 trillion US dollars. This accounts for about 52 percent of the global gross domestic product. Token prices for the Opus model dropped from 15 to 4 US dollars per million tokens. Third party indices show actual transaction prices halved from 1.70 to 0.83 US dollars in one month. The US government recently imposed strict restrictions on remote computing power.

Future token prices for cutting edge models may drop 45 to 55 percent every year. This decline is driven by chip performance doubling and improved model algorithms. The articles leave open whether price reductions will stimulate enough new demand to compensate for losses. It remains uncertain if the intelligence premium can be maintained against open source models. The long term anchor for AI evolution varies from person to person.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA launches Alpamayo 2 Edge reasoning model for autonomous driving on DRIVE Thor hardware
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge on November 22, 2026, to provide autonomous driving capabilities. This compact reasoning vision-language-action model is designed to plan and explain vehicle trajectories. It specifically targets the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor hardware rather than datacenter GPUs. The system aims to provide reasoning-based planning within the compute and latency budgets of onboard hardware.

The 2B-parameter model uses a 2.45B backbone consisting of a 1.96B language model and a 0.41B SigLIP2 encoder. A 0.2B diffusion action expert sits on top, though Hugging Face metadata lists the total as 3B. It processes 22 frames from six cameras and 20 historical ego poses to create 64 waypoints over 6.4 seconds. Real-time use requires the Alpamayo Developer Hub recipe to calibrate FP8 scales and build TensorRT engines.

NVIDIA reports that the model achieves pixel-to-trajectory latency between 160 and 190 milliseconds on DRIVE AGX Thor-X. The company claims the model is a strong closed-loop driver for its size, covering 15.15 kilometers between at-fault incidents in AlpaSim. This performance is described as about 60 times better than the 0.25 kilometers achieved by Qwen-Drive-1.0 4B. The model uses a Chain-of-Causation reasoning trace but emits nominal tokens during routine driving to save compute.

The model was developed using 115,000 hours of multi-camera driving video and 3.7 million reasoning traces. It underwent offline distillation from the larger Alpamayo 2 Super cloud model and closed-loop reinforcement learning in AlpaGym. While validated on a single H100 GPU with 80GB of memory, it requires at least 16 GB for workstation use. Partner Embedl stated that the system reached 10 Hz on AGX Thor in under 48 hours.

stories.Headline: Vocalbeats.AI partners with AI Singapore to give apprentices hands-on AI projects
stories.Summary:
Vocalbeats.AI, a Singapore based AI innovation company, announced a partnership with AI Singapore on November 10, 2026, to support AI talent development. This collaboration officially launched in October 2026 to provide aspiring professionals with hands on industry projects and practical experience in the field. Apprentices will work alongside the Vocalbeats.AI team to apply emerging AI technologies to real business and user needs through practical development projects. The partnership aims to help apprentices strengthen their applied AI skills and deepen their understanding of how AI capabilities become useful applications. This initiative focuses on developing AI engineering capabilities by combining structured training, mentorship, and direct experience with contemporary AI tools and approaches.

The program utilizes the AI Apprenticeship Programme, known as AIAP, which requires apprentices to test solutions against practical requirements and learn from development challenges. Vocalbeats.AI provides industry use cases, practical feedback, and access to its product development experience to support the growth of the local talent pipeline. This effort builds on scholarships established earlier in 2026 at the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, for students. The initiative is supported by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, the Infocomm Media Development Authority, and the National Research Foundation, Singapore. These organizations drive AI Singapore, which brings together research institutions and an ecosystem of AI start ups and companies to power national efforts.

Marco Lai Jinnan, the CEO of Vocalbeats.AI, stated that developing AI talent requires both technical learning and opportunities to apply knowledge to real challenges. He expressed hope that apprentices would gain meaningful exposure to projects and learn from building AI products for a global audience of users. Lai Jinnan noted that this collaboration extends the company's commitment to the talent pipeline and its previous support for university scholarships in Singapore. Laurence Liew, the Director of AI Innovation at AI Singapore, said that industry collaboration helps AI talent translate technical knowledge into practical capability. Liew welcomed the contribution of Vocalbeats.AI in providing hands on learning opportunities for apprentices to tackle real industry challenges and evaluate applications.

The apprentices are the primary group affected, as they gain insight into how AI applications are developed and evaluated through this specific partnership. These individuals will explore contemporary AI tools and learn from the challenges encountered during the development and evaluation of various AI products. The broader ecosystem of AI start ups and companies in Singapore is also involved through the national initiative driven by the government. AI professionals who share an interest in turning emerging technologies into useful products are encouraged to connect with the Vocalbeats.AI global team. The company aims to provide an environment where these professionals can contribute to practical applications and continue developing their professional skills.

Vocalbeats.AI is a Singapore based company dedicated to creating intelligent, user friendly products and services to improve everyday life with accessible voice AI. The company employs an international team of engineers, designers, and researchers to push the boundaries of voice and AI technology for global users. Its expanding portfolio of AI powered applications spans across productivity and wellness to empower people to work smarter and connect more meaningfully. AI Singapore is a national initiative that supports impactful research and develops talent to power the overall AI efforts within the country. The company seeks to redefine how people interact with AI by creating more lifelike and intuitive products for a diverse global user base.

Vocalbeats.AI will continue to develop AI products for global users and provide an environment for AI professionals to contribute to practical applications. The company welcomes individuals interested in applied AI and product development to explore various opportunities with its international team of experts. Future activities include the continued application of emerging AI technologies to meet real business needs and the further development of AI engineering. The articles do not state the specific duration of the partnership or the exact number of apprentices who will participate in the program. It remains open whether additional scholarships will be established at other universities or if new government agencies will join the national initiative.

stories.Headline: Singapore expands AI strategy with new training spots and funding for 500 business projects
stories.Summary:
Singapore announced a major expansion of its artificial intelligence strategy on May 27, 2025, during the ATxEnterprise 2025 conference. Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information Tan Kiat How introduced these initiatives to a group of 200 delegates at the Singapore Expo. The plan involves creating 800 new training opportunities and supporting as many as 500 new projects for 1,000 enterprises. These efforts aim to strengthen the digital economy, which currently accounts for nearly 18 per cent of the local economy.

The training expansion includes 400 places at the national programme AI Singapore, with 300 of those offered through an enhanced AI Apprenticeship Programme over two years. Another 400 spots will be provided by companies including Microsoft, Oracle, Singtel, and Amazon Web Services. AI Singapore will also launch the Pinnacle AI Industry Programme to train 100 expert model builders over three years. For businesses, the GenAI x Digital Leaders initiative will provide funding and guidance for 500 generative AI projects over the next 12 months.

Tan Kiat How stated that technology and artificial intelligence are expected to drive quality economic growth despite global uncertainty. He explained that companies expanding their teams in Singapore will require more practitioners with specialized expertise. The Infocomm Media Development Authority noted that these new roles will add to a current pool of over 6,000 professionals. The agency aims to triple the total tech talent pool to 15,000 by 2028 through various school and upgrading programmes.

The government is acting on concerns from local firms regarding a shortage of artificial intelligence talent. A survey of 350 companies found that 47 per cent believe the local talent pool is insufficient for business needs. To assist further, Alibaba Cloud pledged to help 3,000 small and medium enterprises, while ST Engineering will offer cyber-threat scanning to 2,000 such firms. Prudential Singapore also committed to providing ten generative AI tech explainer videos to support local businesses.

stories.Headline: Analyst Jim Handy warns Samsung and SK hynix face a memory price collapse if AI spending slows
stories.Summary:
Jim Handy, founder and general director of Objective Analysis, warned in an interview with The Korea Times that Samsung Electronics and SK hynix could face a sharp memory price decline if hyperscalers reduce their AI spending. He said memory prices could eventually return to 2024 levels as demand weakens. The warning came as shares of Samsung Electronics and SK hynix fell about 33 percent and 34 percent, respectively, over the past three months until Friday. Handy said a downturn could push chipmakers' gross margins from above 80 percent to near zero within roughly two quarters.

Google, Meta, Amazon and OpenAI are spending roughly 40 percent of their revenue on capital expenditures, including AI computing infrastructure, according to Handy. He said such spending is sustainable only if AI demand keeps growing fast enough to justify the investment. Samsung Electronics posted the world's highest quarterly operating profit in the third quarter, helped by higher orders for high-bandwidth memory and other high-end chips as AI server demand increased. Handy said production levels are limited by demand projections made two years earlier, which he said were lower than subsequent demand.

Handy said he does not think AI demand is growing that quickly, so the hyperscalers are likely to slow their spending at some point, and that will cause memory prices to collapse. He said the growth is temporary and prices will fall back to where they were in 2024. Many Korean analysts have focused on rising production levels as the main threat to prices, but Handy argued the more serious risk could come from the demand side if AI investment fails to maintain its current pace. For Samsung and SK hynix, he said, the key risk is no longer simply whether they can keep up with AI-driven demand, but whether that demand will remain strong enough to absorb the enormous amount of capacity and investment being built around it.

stories.Headline: Google cuts 2027 Broadcom TPU shipments by about 1M units and plans more MediaTek chips, Kuo says
stories.Summary:
Google reportedly reduced its planned 2027 shipments of Broadcom-designed AI chips and prepared to increase shipments of a MediaTek-designed alternative, according to technology supply-chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. Kuo, an analyst at TF International Securities, based the report on an industry survey rather than an official Google announcement. He said his latest industry survey indicated the cut, in a recent post reported on Friday, November 20, 2026. The report concerned Google's custom AI processors, known as Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs. Broadcom shares were down 8.9% on the day amid broad-based selling across the semiconductor sector.

Kuo said Google had cut planned 2027 shipments of its Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by approximately 1 million units, roughly 20% of the series' previously expected shipment volume. Those figures imply a reduction from approximately 5 million chips to 4 million, although both totals are estimates derived from Kuo's reported numbers. Most of the cuts affect the higher-priced 8i Max, also known as Whalefish, according to Kuo. Kuo also reported that Google plans to increase 2027 shipments of the MediaTek-designed TPU 8t series, though the details remain unsettled. The post did not specify the size of that increase, leaving it unclear whether additional 8t shipments would fully offset the reduction in the 8i family.

Kuo linked the change to Google's prioritization of frontier model development, the work involved in building its most advanced AI models. According to his post, Google has repeatedly emphasized in recent months that frontier development receives first call on available computing resources. He characterized the changing TPU shipment mix as an adjustment to that priority amid tight supply chains and data-center power constraints. Kuo's post did not provide pricing, contract terms or an estimate of the financial effect on Broadcom. His post did not provide enough technical or economic detail to establish exactly why Google would favor additional 8t shipments over the affected 8i models.

The report is directionally unfavorable for expectations surrounding Broadcom's Google TPU business and potentially favorable for MediaTek's role in Google's chip plans, though it does not establish the eventual revenue impact for either company. The decline in Broadcom shares should not be attributed solely to the reported shipment changes, and the report adds uncertainty around Broadcom's future Google-related revenue as investors reassess expectations for AI-chip suppliers. A reduction in one chip family does not automatically mean Google expects less overall demand for AI computing, and it could instead reflect a decision to allocate scarce manufacturing capacity, infrastructure and electricity differently. With the shipment changes concerning 2027, the outlook remains subject to revisions. The key questions are how much Google ultimately increases its MediaTek-designed chip orders, whether those gains offset the Broadcom-designed reductions, and what the final mix means for supplier revenue.

The reported changes suggest Google is adjusting the mix of its custom AI processors as it navigates supply-chain constraints and limited data-center power, not necessarily pulling back on its broader AI ambitions. TPUs are Google's custom processors for AI workloads. Kuo is best known for his technology supply-chain research. For now, Kuo's findings point to a potential reshuffling within Google's AI-chip supply chain, not clear evidence of a retreat from AI investment. The concentration of cuts in the higher-priced 8i Max could make the potential revenue impact more significant than the unit reduction alone suggests.
